# Monoline

> Open-source UI kit: a plain CSS core (@monoline/css) with accessible React components (@monoline/react). Three themes, nine accents, font, corner and density options, no Tailwind, no runtime CSS-in-JS.

Start with AGENTS.md (how to work in this repo) and DESIGN.md (the look and rules). Every component is a folder with source, test, demo and meta.json. Install the packages, or copy one component with npx monoline add <name> (source in registry/<name>.json).

## Accordion (accordion)
Stacked headings that each show or hide a section.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Primitive: radix-ui/Accordion | Related: area-chart, avatar, avatar-group
Import: import {Accordion} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<Accordion type="single" collapsible defaultValue="a">
  <AccordionItem value="a"><AccordionTrigger>What is Monoline?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>A small UI kit: plain CSS plus accessible React components.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
  <AccordionItem value="b"><AccordionTrigger>Do I need React?</AccordionTrigger><AccordionContent>No. The CSS works on its own.</AccordionContent></AccordionItem>
</Accordion>
```

A11y:
- Each trigger is a button inside a heading with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Enter and Space toggle; Arrow keys, Home and End move between triggers.
- single or multiple open items; collapsible lets the last one close.

CSS classes: acc-item, acc-header, acc-trigger, acc-content, acc-body, accordion, accordion-body
Data attributes: data-state: open
Source: registry/accordion.json

## Alert (alert)
A message that stays on screen, with a title and a tone.
Status: stable | Category: feedback | Related: empty-state, notification-center, progress
Import: import {Alert} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- tone?: "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger" = 'info' — Meaning of the message: `info` (default), `success`, `warning` or `danger`. `warning` and `danger` are announced at once to screen readers.
- title: ReactNode — The headline of the message. Required: the words carry the meaning, the colour is only extra.
- children?: ReactNode — Optional longer explanation shown under the title.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Alert} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}><Alert title="Synced.">42 entries up to date as of 14:20.</Alert><Alert tone="success" title="Saved.">Your changes are live.</Alert><Alert tone="warning" title="Conflict.">Two devices edited 12 March. Pick which copy to keep.</Alert><Alert tone="danger" title="Can't save.">The folder is read-only. Pick another folder.</Alert></div>
```

A11y:
- danger and warning are role=alert and announced at once; info and success are role=status and polite.
- The title always states the meaning in words; colour is not the only signal.

CSS classes: alert, alert-title, alert-description
Data attributes: data-tone: success | warning | danger
Source: registry/alert.json

## Alert dialog (alert-dialog)
A modal that interrupts to confirm a destructive or irreversible action.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/AlertDialog | Related: command, context-menu, dialog
Import: import {AlertDialog} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {AlertDialog, AlertDialogAction, AlertDialogCancel, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger, Button} from '@monoline/react';

<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger asChild><Button variant="danger">Delete project</Button></AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader><AlertDialogTitle>Delete this project?</AlertDialogTitle><AlertDialogDescription>All files and history are removed. This cannot be undone.</AlertDialogDescription></AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter><AlertDialogCancel>Keep it</AlertDialogCancel><AlertDialogAction>Delete project</AlertDialogAction></AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>
```

A11y:
- role="alertdialog" with a name from the title and a description.
- Focus moves to the Cancel button on open and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape cancels; focus is trapped; the page behind is inert.
- Clicking the overlay does not close it.

CSS classes: dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block
Source: registry/alert-dialog.json

## Animated list (animated-list)
A list whose items enter one by one without shifting the layout.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: bento-grid, border-beam, confetti
Import: import {AnimatedList} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- interval?: number = 300 — Milliseconds between one item entering and the next. Default 300.

Usage:
```tsx
import {AnimatedList} from '@monoline/react';

const row = (t: string, d: string) => (
  <div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s1)', padding: 'var(--s3) var(--s4)', border: '1px solid var(--rule)'}}>
    <strong>{t}</strong><span style={{color: 'var(--muted)', fontSize: 'var(--text-sm)'}}>{d}</span>
  </div>
);

<AnimatedList style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s2)', maxWidth: '24rem'}}>
  {row('Build passed', 'main, 2 minutes ago')}
  {row('Review requested', 'Docs update, 5 minutes ago')}
  {row('Deploy finished', 'Production, 9 minutes ago')}
</AnimatedList>
```

A11y:
- A real <ul> with <li> items, so list semantics and counts are announced.
- Items fade in with opacity only and keep their space from the first frame; there is no layout shift.
- With prefers-reduced-motion all items are visible at once.

CSS classes: animated-list, animated-list-item
Source: registry/animated-list.json

## Area chart (area-chart)
A line chart filled down to zero, optionally stacked to show a running total.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, avatar, avatar-group
Import: import {AreaChart} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- stacked?: boolean — Stack series on top of each other so the top edge is the running total.
- showPoints?: boolean — Mark each data point. A single point is always marked.

Usage:
```tsx
import {AreaChart} from '@monoline/react';

const months = ['Jan', 'Feb', 'Mar', 'Apr', 'May', 'Jun'];

<AreaChart title="Active users" labels={months} series={[{name: 'Users', values: [120, 180, 150, 240, 310, 290]}]} />
```

A11y:
- The chart is role=img with the required title as its name.
- A visually hidden table lists every value, one row per category, for screen readers.
- One focusable stop per category with a spoken label; Arrow keys move between them and Escape hides the tooltip.
- The value tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus; stacked charts also show the total.
- Series differ by fill pattern and dash as well as colour, and the legend names them.
- No entrance animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: chart, chart-plot, chart-svg, chart-hits, chart-s0, chart-s1, chart-s2, chart-s3, chart-s4, chart-tick, chart-value, chart-rule, chart-zero, chart-outline, chart-pat, chart-pat-dot, chart-line, chart-area, chart-hit, chart-tip, chart-tip-title, chart-tip-row, chart-tip-value, chart-legend, chart-legend-detail, chart-swatch, chart-empty, chart-marks, chart-point, chart-guide
Data attributes: data-active; data-align: start | end
Source: registry/area-chart.json

## Aspect ratio (aspect-ratio)
Keep media or a placeholder at a fixed width-to-height ratio.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Primitive: radix-ui/AspectRatio | Related: box, container, direction-provider
Import: import {AspectRatio} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {AspectRatio} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{width: '320px'}}><AspectRatio ratio={16 / 9}><div style={{width: '100%', height: '100%', border: '1px solid var(--rule)', display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center'}}>16:9</div></AspectRatio></div>
```

A11y:
- A plain div; the content keeps its own semantics and alt text.
Source: registry/aspect-ratio.json

## Autocomplete (autocomplete)
A text field that suggests values while you type and accepts anything you enter.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: field
Import: import {Autocomplete} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- suggestions: string[] — Suggestions shown while typing; matched by substring, case-insensitive.
- value?: string — The text in the field.
- defaultValue?: string = '' — Initial text when the field is uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the text on every change, and with the suggestion when one is picked.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Autocomplete, Field} from '@monoline/react';

const cities = ['Amsterdam', 'Berlin', 'Bangalore', 'Boston', 'Lisbon', 'London', 'Lagos'];

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px', minHeight: '220px'}}><Field label="City"><Autocomplete suggestions={cities} placeholder="Start typing" /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- ARIA 1.2 combobox with aria-autocomplete="list", aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp move through suggestions, Enter picks the active one (or keeps typed text), Escape closes.
- The field value is always the typed or picked text; nothing is forced to match a suggestion.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, autocomplete, autocomplete-list, autocomplete-option
Data attributes: data-active
Source: registry/autocomplete.json

## Avatar (avatar)
A person or thing as an image with an initials fallback.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Primitive: radix-ui/Avatar | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar-group
Import: import {Avatar} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- src?: string — Image URL. If it fails or is missing, the initials show.
- name: string — The person's name. Used as the image alt text and to make initials; required so it always has a name.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense rows or `lg`.
- variant?: "line" | "solid" = 'solid' — `solid` (default) fills the circle; `line` draws only an outline.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Avatar} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', alignItems: 'center'}}><Avatar name="Ada Lovelace" /><Avatar name="Grace Hopper" variant="line" /><Avatar name="Alan Turing" size="lg" /></div>
```

A11y:
- name is required: it is the image alt text and the fallback's accessible name.
- The fallback shows while the image loads or if it fails.

CSS classes: avatar, avatar-sm, avatar-lg, avatar-line, avatar-group, tag, stat, stat-value, stat-note
Source: registry/avatar.json

## Avatar group (avatar-group)
Overlap several avatars and show how many more there are.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: avatar
Import: import {AvatarGroup} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label: string — Names the group, for example "Project members".
- max?: number = 4 — Show at most this many avatars, then "+N".

Usage:
```tsx
import {Avatar, AvatarGroup} from '@monoline/react';

<AvatarGroup aria-label="Project members" max={3}>{['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Linus Torvalds'].map((n) => <Avatar key={n} name={n} />)}</AvatarGroup>
```

A11y:
- role="group" with an accessible name; the overflow count is plain text.

CSS classes: avatar, avatar-sm, avatar-lg, avatar-line, avatar-group, tag, stat, stat-value, stat-note
Source: registry/avatar-group.json

## Badge (badge)
A short status word or count.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Badge} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- variant?: "solid" | "outline" | "accent" = 'outline' — `accent` only for "new" or "now".

Usage:
```tsx
import {Badge} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', flexWrap: 'wrap'}}><Badge>draft</Badge><Badge variant="solid">12 days</Badge><Badge variant="accent">new</Badge></div>
```

A11y:
- Plain text in a span; the word carries the meaning, not the colour.
- For a count that changes, put it inside an aria-live region yourself.

CSS classes: swatch, check, check-pass, check-fail, badge, badge-solid, badge-accent, kbd, key-hints, dot, heat-0, heat-1, heat-2, heat-3, heat-4
Source: registry/badge.json

## Bar chart (bar-chart)
Compare values across categories with vertical or horizontal bars, grouped or stacked.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {BarChart} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: string — Accessible name and table caption. Required.
- data?: ChartDatum[] — One series: `[{label: 'Mon', value: 3}]`.
- series?: ChartSeries[] — Several series: `[{name: 'Visits', values: [3, 5]}]`, with `labels` for the categories.
- labels?: string[] — Category labels for the x axis (or y axis when horizontal), one per value in `series`.
- seriesName?: string = 'Value' — Name of the single series when `data` is used. Default "Value".
- orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal" = 'vertical' — `vertical` draws columns, `horizontal` draws rows (better for long labels). Default `vertical`.
- stacked?: boolean = false — Stack series on top of each other instead of side by side.
- showValues?: boolean = false — Print each value at the end of its bar (the total for stacked bars).
- height?: number — Chart height in px. Horizontal charts size themselves to the number of rows when omitted. Default 280.
- valueFormat?: ((value: number) => string) — Format a value for labels, tooltips and the table.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BarChart} from '@monoline/react';

const week = [{label: 'Mon', value: 12}, {label: 'Tue', value: 19}, {label: 'Wed', value: 9}, {label: 'Thu', value: 24}, {label: 'Fri', value: 17}, {label: 'Sat', value: 6}, {label: 'Sun', value: 4}];

<BarChart title="Signups per weekday" data={week} showValues />
```

A11y:
- The chart is role=img with the required title as its name.
- A visually hidden table lists every value, one row per category, for screen readers.
- One focusable stop per category with a spoken label; Arrow keys move between them and Escape hides the tooltip.
- The value tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus.
- Series differ by fill pattern as well as colour, and the legend names them.
- No entrance animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: chart, chart-plot, chart-svg, chart-hits, chart-s0, chart-s1, chart-s2, chart-s3, chart-s4, chart-tick, chart-value, chart-rule, chart-zero, chart-outline, chart-pat, chart-pat-dot, chart-line, chart-area, chart-hit, chart-tip, chart-tip-title, chart-tip-row, chart-tip-value, chart-legend, chart-legend-detail, chart-swatch, chart-empty, chart-marks, chart-bar
Data attributes: data-active; data-align: start | end
Source: registry/bar-chart.json

## Bento grid (bento-grid)
A responsive asymmetric grid of cards with column and row spans.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, border-beam, confetti
Import: import {BentoGrid} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- colSpan?: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 — Columns to span once the grid has room for them. Default 1.
- rowSpan?: 1 | 2 = 1 — Rows to span. Default 1.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BentoCard, BentoGrid} from '@monoline/react';

const tile = (title: string, text: string) => (<><h3 style={{margin: 0, fontWeight: 500}}>{title}</h3><p style={{margin: 'var(--s2) 0 0', color: 'var(--muted)'}}>{text}</p></>);

<BentoGrid>
  <BentoCard colSpan={2} rowSpan={2}>{tile('Tokens first', 'Every colour, space and rule comes from one small set of tokens.')}</BentoCard>
  <BentoCard>{tile('Three themes', 'Warm, dark and midnight.')}</BentoCard>
  <BentoCard>{tile('Four accents', 'One accent at a time.')}</BentoCard>
  <BentoCard colSpan={3}>{tile('Plain CSS core', 'Use the stylesheets alone, or the React layer on top.')}</BentoCard>
</BentoGrid>
```

A11y:
- Plain divs in source order, so reading and tab order match the visual order on phones and follow the DOM elsewhere.
- Spans collapse to a single column on narrow screens; nothing depends on colour or motion.

CSS classes: bento-grid, bento-card, bento-col-2, bento-col-3, bento-row-2
Source: registry/bento-grid.json

## Call to action block (block-cta)
A closing call to action with one sentence and one next step.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, heading, text, button
Import: import {BlockCta} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: ReactNode — The one-sentence call to action, rendered as the section heading.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted supporting line under the title.
- actions: ReactNode — The next step: a solid Button and maybe a line one.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 = 2 — Outline level of the title, 1 to 5. Default 2.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockCta, Button} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockCta title="Start building today" description="Install the package and copy your first component." actions={<><Button variant="solid">Get started</Button><Button>Read the docs</Button></>} />
```

A11y:
- A section named by its title; actions are ordinary buttons or links.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, block-cta, block-cta-box, block-cta-copy, block-cta-actions
Source: registry/block-cta.json

## Dashboard shell block (block-dashboard-shell)
App frame with sidebar, top bar and content that collapses to a drawer on small screens.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, stack, drawer, button
Import: import {BlockDashboardShell} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- brand?: ReactNode — Your logo or name, shown above the navigation.
- renderLink?: RenderLink — Renders each navigation link, so a client router can handle the click. Default a plain `<a href>`.
- nav: ShellNavItem[] — The navigation links shown in the sidebar and in the small-screen drawer.
- navLabel?: string = 'Main' — Names the navigation landmark. Default "Main".
- topbar?: ReactNode — Right side of the top bar: search, account menu.
- menuLabel?: string = 'Menu' — Text of the button that opens the navigation drawer on small screens. Default "Menu".
- children: ReactNode — The page: put its h1 inside.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Badge, BlockDashboardShell, Heading, Text} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockDashboardShell
  brand="Your app"
  nav={[{label: 'Overview', href: '#', current: true}, {label: 'Reports', href: '#'}, {label: 'Customers', href: '#'}, {label: 'Settings', href: '#'}]}
  topbar={<Badge>Ada Example</Badge>}
>
  <Heading level={1} size="xl">Overview</Heading>
  <Text tone="muted">Your content goes here.</Text>
</BlockDashboardShell>
```

A11y:
- The sidebar and the drawer hold the same navigation landmark, named by navLabel; the current page has aria-current="page".
- Below 800px the sidebar is hidden and a Menu button opens a left drawer: focus is trapped, Escape closes it and focus returns to the button.
- Choosing a link closes the drawer. The content is a main landmark; put one h1 in it.
- With renderLink the links are rendered by your router link; the block still sets the class and aria-current="page" on it.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, stack, stack-row, stack-wrap, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title, drawer-content, block-shell, block-shell-side, block-shell-brand, block-shell-nav, block-shell-link, block-shell-body, block-shell-top, block-shell-top-end, block-shell-content, block-shell-menu
Data attributes: data-align: start | center | end | stretch; data-justify: start | center | end | between; data-side: right | end | left | start | top | bottom
Source: registry/block-dashboard-shell.json

## Empty page block (block-empty-page)
A full-page message for not found, nothing yet or no access.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: heading, text
Import: import {BlockEmptyPage} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- code?: ReactNode — A short code such as "404" or "Empty". Decorative.
- title: ReactNode — The message headline, for example "Page not found".
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted sentence explaining what happened or what to do next.
- actions?: ReactNode — The way out: a solid Button or link, and maybe a second.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 — Outline level of the title. A full-page empty state is usually the page's h1.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockEmptyPage, Button} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockEmptyPage code="404" title="Page not found" description="The address may be wrong, or the page moved." actions={<><Button variant="solid">Go home</Button><Button>Contact support</Button></>} />
```

A11y:
- A section named by its title, with the title as the page heading.
- The large code is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.

CSS classes: heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, block-empty-page, block-empty-page-code, block-empty-page-description, block-empty-page-actions
Source: registry/block-empty-page.json

## Feature grid block (block-feature-grid)
A section title above a responsive grid of short features.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, heading, text
Import: import {BlockFeatureGrid} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: ReactNode — Section heading shown above the grid.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted line under the section heading.
- features: Feature[] — The items to show, each with a `title`, `description` and optional `icon`.
- columns?: 2 | 3 | 4 = 3 — Number of columns on wide screens: 2, 3 (default) or 4. Fewer columns are used on narrow screens.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 = 2 — Outline level of the section title; each feature title is one level lower.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockFeatureGrid} from '@monoline/react';

const dot = <svg width="20" height="20" viewBox="0 0 20 20" fill="none" stroke="currentColor"><rect x="3" y="3" width="14" height="14" /></svg>;

const features = [
  {title: 'Plain CSS', description: 'Works with any framework, or none.', icon: dot},
  {title: 'Accessible', description: 'Keyboard and screen reader behaviour is tested.', icon: dot},
  {title: 'Three themes', description: 'Warm, dark and midnight, one accent.', icon: dot},
  {title: 'Copy and own', description: 'Every component is one small folder.', icon: dot},
  {title: 'Typed', description: 'Props are string unions with sane defaults.', icon: dot},
  {title: 'No runtime styling', description: 'Tokens and classes only.', icon: dot},
];

<BlockFeatureGrid title="Why Monoline" description="Fewer parts, clearer pages." features={features} />
```

A11y:
- A section named by its title; features are a list of items.
- Feature titles are headings one level below the section title, so the outline stays in order.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, block-features, block-features-head, block-features-grid, block-feature, block-feature-icon
Data attributes: data-columns: 3 | 4
Source: registry/block-feature-grid.json

## Footer block (block-footer)
A site footer with brand, link columns and small print.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, link
Import: import {BlockFooter} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- brand?: ReactNode — Your logo or name.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional short sentence about the product, shown under the brand.
- columns: FooterColumn[] — Groups of links; each column has a `title` and a list of `links` and becomes its own labelled `nav`.
- renderLink?: RenderLink — Renders each link, so a client router can handle the click. Default a plain `<a href>`.
- legal?: ReactNode — Small print: copyright, legal links.
- headingLevel?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 — Outline level of the column titles.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockFooter} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockFooter
  brand="Your brand"
  description="Short line about what you make."
  columns={[
    {title: 'Product', links: [{label: 'Components', href: '#'}, {label: 'Blocks', href: '#'}, {label: 'Changelog', href: '#'}]},
    {title: 'Resources', links: [{label: 'Docs', href: '#'}, {label: 'Source', href: '#'}]},
    {title: 'Company', links: [{label: 'About', href: '#'}, {label: 'Contact', href: '#'}]},
  ]}
  legal="© 2026 Your brand. All rights reserved."
/>
```

A11y:
- A footer element: the page contentinfo landmark. Use one per page.
- Each link column is a nav named by its title, with a heading at the chosen level.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, link, block-footer, block-footer-top, block-footer-brand, block-footer-name, block-footer-columns, block-footer-heading, block-footer-col, block-footer-legal
Source: registry/block-footer.json

## Hero block (block-hero)
A page opener with eyebrow, title, description, actions and optional media.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, heading, text
Import: import {BlockHero} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- eyebrow?: ReactNode — Optional small line above the title, for example a category or announcement.
- title: ReactNode — The main headline of the page.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted supporting text under the title.
- actions?: ReactNode — Buttons or links. Make one of them the solid Button.
- media?: ReactNode — An image, screenshot or illustration shown beside (wide) or below (narrow) the copy.
- align?: "center" | "start" = 'start' — `start` (default) left-aligns the copy; `center` centres it.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 — Outline level of the title. A hero is usually the page's h1.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockHero, Button} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockHero
  eyebrow="Version 1.0"
  title="Interfaces with fewer parts"
  description="A small kit of plain components. Copy the ones you need."
  actions={<><Button variant="solid">Get started</Button><Button>Read the docs</Button></>}
  media={<div style={{border: '1px solid var(--rule)', aspectRatio: '4 / 3', display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center'}}>Preview</div>}
/>
```

A11y:
- A section named by its title through aria-labelledby.
- The title is a real heading; headingLevel sets the outline level (h1 by default).
- Media is passed in: give images alt text.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, block-hero, block-hero-inner, block-hero-copy, block-hero-eyebrow, block-hero-description, block-hero-actions, block-hero-media
Data attributes: data-align: center
Source: registry/block-hero.json

Email and password sign-in form with validation messages.

- submitLabel?: ReactNode = 'Sign in' — Text of the submit button. Default "Sign in".

A11y:

## Pricing block (block-pricing)
Plan cards with a monthly and yearly switch.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: container, heading, text, button, badge, segmented-control
Import: import {BlockPricing} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: ReactNode — Section heading shown above the tiers.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted line under the heading.
- tiers: PricingTier[] — The plans to compare, each with a name, monthly and yearly price, features and a call to action.
- defaultInterval?: PricingInterval = 'monthly' — Start on yearly billing.
- labels?: Partial<{ monthly: string; yearly: string; switcher: string; period: Record<PricingInterval, string>; highlight: string; }> — Overrides for the built-in English texts (Monthly, Yearly, Billing period, Popular, / month, / year); use it to translate.
- renderLink?: RenderLink — Renders a tier's link (the ones with `href`), so a client router can handle the click. Default a plain `<a href>`.
- onSelect?: ((tier: PricingTier, interval: PricingInterval) => void) — Called when a tier's button (one without `href`) is pressed.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 = 2 — Outline level of the section title, 1 to 5. Default 2; each tier name is one level lower.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockPricing} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockPricing
  title="Simple pricing"
  description="Switch to yearly for two months free."
  tiers={[
    {name: 'Free', description: 'For trying it out.', price: {monthly: '$0', yearly: '$0'}, features: ['One project', 'Community support'], ctaLabel: 'Start free', href: '#'},
    {name: 'Team', description: 'For small teams.', price: {monthly: '$12', yearly: '$120'}, features: ['Unlimited projects', 'Email support', 'Shared themes'], ctaLabel: 'Choose Team', highlighted: true},
    {name: 'Scale', description: 'For larger groups.', price: {monthly: '$48', yearly: '$480'}, features: ['Everything in Team', 'Single sign-on', 'Priority support'], ctaLabel: 'Talk to us', href: '#'},
  ]}
/>
```

A11y:
- A section named by its title; plans are a list, each with a heading one level below the title.
- The billing switch is a named radio group operable with arrow keys.
- Prices are plain text next to their period, never colour alone; the popular plan carries a text badge.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full, heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, swatch, check, check-pass, check-fail, badge, badge-solid, badge-accent, kbd, key-hints, dot, heat-0, heat-1, heat-2, heat-3, heat-4, segmented, segment, block-pricing, block-pricing-head, block-pricing-tiers, block-tier, block-tier-head, block-tier-price, block-tier-amount, block-tier-period, block-tier-features
Data attributes: data-state: on; data-highlighted

## Settings form block (block-settings-form)
Settings sections of switches and selects, each in a fieldset.
Status: beta | Category: blocks | Related: form, fieldset, switch, native-select, field, button, heading
Import: import {BlockSettingsForm} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: ReactNode — Heading of the settings page.
- description?: ReactNode — Optional muted line under the heading.
- sections: SettingsSection[] — The groups of settings; each has a `legend`, optional `description` and a list of switch or select `items`.
- saveLabel?: ReactNode = 'Save changes' — Text of the submit button. Default "Save changes".
- resetLabel?: ReactNode = 'Reset' — Text of the button that restores the initial values. Default "Reset".
- onSubmit?: ((values: Record<string, string | boolean>) => void) — Called with every control's value: switches are `true` or `false`, selects their value.
- loading?: boolean — Shows a spinner on the save button while you save.
- headingLevel?: 1 | 2 | 3 = 1 — Outline level of the title, 1 to 3. Default 1.

Usage:
```tsx
import {BlockSettingsForm} from '@monoline/react';

<BlockSettingsForm
  title="Settings"
  description="Changes apply to your account."
  sections={[
    {legend: 'Notifications', description: 'Choose what we email you.', items: [
      {kind: 'switch', name: 'product', label: 'Product updates', hint: 'About once a month.', defaultChecked: true},
      {kind: 'switch', name: 'digest', label: 'Weekly digest'},
    ]},
    {legend: 'Display', items: [
      {kind: 'select', name: 'theme', label: 'Theme', options: [{value: 'warm', label: 'Warm'}, {value: 'dark', label: 'Dark'}, {value: 'midnight', label: 'Midnight'}], defaultValue: 'warm'},
      {kind: 'select', name: 'density', label: 'Density', hint: 'Compact fits more rows.', options: [{value: 'comfortable', label: 'Comfortable'}, {value: 'compact', label: 'Compact'}]},
    ]},
  ]}
/>
```

A11y:
- Each section is a fieldset with a legend, so grouped controls are announced with it.
- Switches have role=switch with visible labels; hints are linked with aria-describedby.
- Selects are native and labelled.

CSS classes: form, form-errors, form-errors-title, form-actions, fieldset, fieldset-legend, checkbox, radio, sw, checkbox-mark, radio-dot, radio-group, sw-thumb, choice, choice-group, field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, field-error, field-ok, input-group, input-affix, field-required, form-row, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, spinner, skeleton, skeleton-block, skeleton-hatch, heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm, text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate, block-settings, block-settings-head, block-settings-row

## Box (box)
A div with padding and a thin border mapped to the spacing tokens.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, container, direction-provider
Import: import {Box} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- padding?: Step — Padding on all sides: a step on the spacing scale (1 = --s1 up to 9).
- paddingX?: Step — Horizontal padding (left and right) as a step 1 to 9 on the spacing scale; overrides `padding` on that axis.
- paddingY?: Step — Vertical padding (top and bottom) as a step 1 to 9 on the spacing scale; overrides `padding` on that axis.
- border?: boolean | "start" | "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "end" — A thin rule on every side (`true`) or on one side.
- asChild?: boolean — Render the child (a `section`, `aside`, `li`) with the box styles.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Box} from '@monoline/react';

<Box padding={5} border>A bordered box with step 5 padding.</Box>
```

A11y:
- A plain element; adds no roles. Use asChild to render a landmark such as section.

CSS classes: box, box-border
Data attributes: data-border: top | right | end | bottom | left | start
Source: registry/box.json

## Breadcrumb (breadcrumb)
The path to the current page.
Status: stable | Category: navigation | Related: menubar, navigation-menu, pagination
Import: import {Breadcrumb} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- items: BreadcrumbItem[] — The trail from the root to the current page; the last item is treated as the current page and is not a link.
- aria-label?: string — Name of the landmark.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Breadcrumb} from '@monoline/react';

<Breadcrumb items={[{label: 'Home', href: '#'}, {label: 'Projects', href: '#'}, {label: 'Monoline'}]} />
```

A11y:
- A nav landmark with an aria-label, containing an ordered list.
- The current page has aria-current=page and is not a link.

CSS classes: crumbs, pager, steps, step, topbar, brand, topbar-nav, tab, tabpanel, link, divider, skip-link
Data attributes: data-state: done
Source: registry/breadcrumb.json

## Button (button)
Triggers an action. Native button with solid, line, ghost and danger variants.
Status: stable | Category: buttons | Primitive: radix-ui/Slot | Related: button-group, copy-button, icon-button
Import: import {Button} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- variant?: "danger" | "line" | "solid" | "ghost" = 'line' — `solid` is the one main action per view. `line` for the rest, `ghost` for inline links, `danger` for destructive.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense toolbars and table rows, or `lg` for prominent calls to action. Same heights as Input and Select.
- loading?: boolean = false — Shows a spinner, sets `aria-busy` and ignores clicks. The label stays so the width does not jump.
- asChild?: boolean = false — Render the child element (a link, a router link) with the button styles instead of a `<button>`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', flexWrap: 'wrap'}}>
  <Button variant="solid">Write today</Button>
  <Button variant="line">Open folder</Button>
  <Button variant="ghost">Show all</Button>
  <Button variant="danger">Delete entry</Button>
</div>
```

A11y:
- Native <button>: Enter and Space activate, Tab focuses.
- loading sets aria-busy and blocks clicks while keeping the label.
- asChild renders a link without losing link semantics.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, spinner, skeleton, skeleton-block, skeleton-hatch
Source: registry/button.json

## Calendar (calendar)
A month grid for picking one date.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, checkbox, color-picker
Import: import {Calendar} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: Date | null — The selected date when controlled; `null` means none. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: Date | null = null — The initially selected date when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onValueChange?: ((date: Date | null) => void) — Called with the date the user picks, or `null` when the user presses "Clear date" (only with `clearable`).
- clearable?: boolean = false — Adds a "Clear date" button under the grid that resets the value to `null`. Default false.
- weekStartsOn?: 0 | 1 = 0 — First day of the week: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.
- min?: Date — Earliest selectable date; earlier days are disabled.
- max?: Date — Latest selectable date; later days are disabled.
- locale?: string — BCP 47 locale for month and day names.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Calendar} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [d, setD] = useState<Date | null>(null);
  return <div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s3)', justifyItems: 'start'}}><Calendar value={d} onValueChange={setD} weekStartsOn={1} /><p className="muted small" role="status">{d ? d.toDateString() : 'No date picked'}</p></div>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- role="grid" with column headers; one day is in the tab order (roving tabindex).
- Arrow keys move by day and week, Home/End to the start and end of the week, PageUp/PageDown by month.
- Each day button has a full date name; the selected day has aria-pressed and today has aria-current="date".
- With `clearable`, a "Clear date" button resets the value; it is disabled while no date is chosen.

CSS classes: calendar, calendar-head, calendar-title, calendar-nav, calendar-grid, calendar-day
Data attributes: data-outside; data-today
Source: registry/calendar.json

## Card (card)
A bordered group for one thing you can pick up or open.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Primitive: radix-ui/Slot | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Card} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- interactive?: boolean — Adds a hover outline. Use with `asChild` on a link or button so the whole card is one control.
- asChild?: boolean — Render the child element (a link, an `article`) with the card styles instead of a `div`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardFooter, CardHeader, CardTitle} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: 360}}><Card><CardHeader><CardTitle>Ship the pricing page</CardTitle><CardDescription>Today, 14:20 · 3 files</CardDescription></CardHeader><CardContent><p>Rewrote the headline and the plan table.</p></CardContent><CardFooter><Button variant="solid" size="sm">Open</Button><Button size="sm">Share</Button></CardFooter></Card></div>
```

A11y:
- Plain divs and a heading; no roles added.
- With asChild on a link or button the whole card is one keyboard-focusable control.

CSS classes: card, card-hover, banner, banner-accent, banner-warning, banner-danger, card-header, card-title, card-description, card-content, card-footer
Source: registry/card.json

## Checkbox (checkbox)

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- label?: ReactNode — Visible label. Without it, give the checkbox an `aria-label`.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the checkbox as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

```tsx
import {Checkbox} from '@monoline/react';
```

## Code block (code-block)
A block of code with a copy button.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {CodeBlock} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- code: string — The text to show and to copy. Rendered as text with coloured spans, never as HTML.
- title?: string — A file name (`button.tsx`) or label (`bash`) shown in the header. Also names the region and picks the language.
- language?: Language — Syntax colouring: `tsx`, `ts`, `jsx`, `js`, `css`, `html`, `bash`, `json` or `text`. Default: guessed from `title`, else `text`.
- lineNumbers?: boolean — Number each line. Use for longer listings, not one-line commands.
- hideCopy?: boolean — Hide the copy button.

Usage:
```tsx
import {CodeBlock} from '@monoline/react';

const tsx = `import {Button} from '@monoline/react';

export function Save() {
  // One solid button per view.
  return <Button variant="solid" onClick={() => save(42)}>Save</Button>;
}`;

<CodeBlock title="save.tsx" code={tsx} />
```

A11y:
- The code is a pre/code element; the region has an accessible name.
- The copy button is announced as "Copy code" and confirms with a polite live message.

CSS classes: code-block, code-head, code-title, code-copy, code-line, tok-keyword, tok-string, tok-number, tok-comment, tok-tag, tok-attr, tok-fn, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block
Data attributes: data-copied; data-headless; data-lines
Source: registry/code-block.json

## Collapsible (collapsible)
Show or hide one region of content from a trigger.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Primitive: radix-ui/Collapsible | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Collapsible} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Collapsible, CollapsibleContent, CollapsibleTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<Collapsible><CollapsibleTrigger asChild><Button size="sm">Show details</Button></CollapsibleTrigger><CollapsibleContent><p>Extra detail appears here when the trigger is pressed.</p></CollapsibleContent></Collapsible>
```

A11y:
- The trigger is a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls.
- Space and Enter toggle it.

CSS classes: collapsible-content
Source: registry/collapsible.json

## Color picker (color-picker)
Choose a colour from preset swatches, the native colour control, or a hex value.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: input
Import: import {ColorPicker} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: string — The colour as "#rrggbb".
- defaultValue?: string = '#000000' — The initial colour as "#rrggbb" when uncontrolled.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the new colour as "#rrggbb" when the user picks a swatch or types a valid hex.
- colors?: string[] = PRESETS — Preset swatches, each a CSS hex colour. Set from this prop, never from the stylesheet.
- disabled?: boolean — Stops the user changing the colour.
- aria-label?: string — Accessible name for the group.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {ColorPicker} from '@monoline/react';

function Controlled() {
  const [c, setC] = useState('#0090ff');
  return <div style={{maxWidth: '280px'}}><ColorPicker aria-label="Brand colour" value={c} onValueChange={setC} /><p>Chosen: {c}</p></div>;
}

<Controlled />
```

A11y:
- A group with an accessible name; each swatch is a button named by its hex value, with aria-pressed for the current colour.
- The native colour input and the hex text field each have their own name.
- The hex field sets aria-invalid and points to an error message with aria-describedby until the value is valid; colour is never the only signal because the hex text is always shown.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, color-picker, color-picker-swatches, color-picker-swatch, color-picker-row, color-picker-native, color-picker-hex, color-picker-error
Data attributes: data-disabled
Source: registry/color-picker.json

## Combobox (combobox)
Type to filter a list and pick one option.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: field
Import: import {Combobox} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- options: ComboboxOption[] — The choices, each with a `value`, a `label` and an optional `disabled`. The user filters them by typing part of the label.
- value?: string — The selected option's `value` when controlled; `''` means none. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string = '' — The initially selected option's `value` when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the chosen option's value, or '' when cleared.
- emptyText?: string = 'No matches' — Shown when nothing matches.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Combobox, Field} from '@monoline/react';

const options = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Linus Torvalds'].map((n) => ({value: n.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, '-'), label: n}));

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px', minHeight: '260px'}}><Field label="Person"><Combobox options={options} placeholder="Type a name" /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- ARIA 1.2 combobox: the input has role="combobox" with aria-expanded, aria-controls and aria-activedescendant.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp move through options, Enter picks, Escape closes (and clears the typed text on a second press), Tab leaves.
- Options are in a listbox with aria-selected; an empty result is announced as text.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, combobox, combobox-list, combobox-option, combobox-empty
Data attributes: data-active
Source: registry/combobox.json

## Command (command)
A searchable palette of actions that opens over the page, with an optional global shortcut.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/Dialog | Related: alert-dialog, context-menu, dialog
Import: import {Command} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- items: CommandItem[] — The actions to list, each with an `id`, `label` and optional `group`, `keywords`, `hint`, `disabled` and `onSelect`.
- open?: boolean — Whether the palette is open when controlled. Pair with `onOpenChange`.
- defaultOpen?: boolean = false — Whether the palette starts open when uncontrolled. Default false.
- onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Called with the new open state when the palette opens or closes.
- shortcut?: string — A global key that toggles the palette, like `mod+k` (`mod` is Cmd on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere).
- title?: string = 'Command palette' — Names the dialog. Visually hidden.
- placeholder?: string = 'Type a command' — Placeholder text of the search box. Default "Type a command".
- emptyText?: string = 'No results' — Message shown when no item matches the search. Default "No results".
- trigger?: ReactNode — Optional trigger element, rendered as-is (use a Button with aria-haspopup="dialog").
- className?: string — Extra class name for the palette panel.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Command, type CommandItem} from '@monoline/react';

const items: CommandItem[] = [
  {id: 'new', label: 'New file', group: 'File', hint: 'N'},
  {id: 'open', label: 'Open file', group: 'File', hint: 'O', keywords: ['browse']},
  {id: 'save', label: 'Save', group: 'File', hint: 'S'},
  {id: 'theme', label: 'Switch theme', group: 'View', keywords: ['dark', 'light']},
  {id: 'zoom', label: 'Zoom in', group: 'View'},
  {id: 'help', label: 'Open help'},
];

<Command shortcut="mod+k" items={items} trigger={<button type="button" className="btn btn-outline">Open palette</button>} />
```

A11y:
- A modal dialog named by a hidden title; focus moves to the search input and returns to the opener on close.
- The input is an ARIA combobox controlling a listbox of grouped options; focus stays in the input and aria-activedescendant names the active option.
- ArrowUp and ArrowDown move (skipping disabled items), Home and End jump, Enter runs the item, Escape closes.
- The shortcut prop toggles the palette from anywhere (mod is Cmd on Mac, Ctrl elsewhere); result count is announced through a status region.

CSS classes: dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title, command, command-input, command-list, command-heading, command-item, command-hint, command-empty
Data attributes: data-active
Source: registry/command.json

## Confetti (confetti)
A short burst of square confetti on a canvas, triggered by a prop or a ref method.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: button
Import: import {Confetti} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- burst?: number — Fires a burst each time this number changes (not on mount). Or call `ref.current.fire()`.
- count?: number = 60 — Pieces per burst. Default 60.
- origin?: { x: number; y: number; } = {x: 0.5, y: 0.5} — Where the burst starts, as 0 to 1 of the window. Default the centre.
- colors?: string[] — Fill colours. Default: the accent, foreground and muted tokens.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useRef} from 'react';
import {Button, Confetti, type ConfettiHandle} from '@monoline/react';

function Fire() {
  const ref = useRef<ConfettiHandle>(null);
  return (
    <>
      <Confetti ref={ref} />
      <Button variant="line" onClick={() => ref.current?.fire()}>Celebrate</Button>
    </>
  );
}

<Fire />
```

A11y:
- The canvas is aria-hidden and ignores the pointer, so it never blocks or announces anything.
- Off under prefers-reduced-motion: no burst is drawn. Announce the event it celebrates in text as well.

CSS classes: confetti
Source: registry/confetti.json

## Container (container)
Centre content in a column with a sensible maximum width and side padding.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, box, direction-provider
Import: import {Container} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- size?: "text" | "page" | "full" = 'page' — `text` is a reading column, `page` the widest main column, `full` no limit.
- asChild?: boolean — Render the child (a `main`, `section`) with the container styles.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Container} from '@monoline/react';

<Container size="text"><p>A column about 64 characters wide, centred, with side padding.</p></Container>
```

A11y:
- A plain div; adds no roles.

CSS classes: container, container-text, container-page, container-full
Source: registry/container.json

## Context menu (context-menu)
A menu of actions opened by right click or long press on an area.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/ContextMenu | Related: alert-dialog, command, dialog
Import: import {ContextMenu} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- tone?: "danger" | "default" = 'default' — `danger` highlights in the danger colour.

Usage:
```tsx
import {ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuLabel, ContextMenuSeparator, ContextMenuTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger><div style={{display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center', height: '120px', border: '1px dashed var(--rule)'}}>Right click here</div></ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent><ContextMenuLabel>File</ContextMenuLabel><ContextMenuItem>Rename</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuItem>Duplicate</ContextMenuItem><ContextMenuSeparator /><ContextMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</ContextMenuItem></ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>
```

A11y:
- Opens with right click, long press or the context-menu key (Shift+F10).
- Arrow keys move, Enter or Space selects, Escape closes and returns focus.
- Every action must also exist elsewhere in the UI for people who cannot open it.

CSS classes: popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, dropdown, menu, menu-end, danger, menu-sep
Data attributes: data-highlighted; data-disabled; data-variant: danger
Source: registry/context-menu.json

## Copy button (copy-button)
A button that copies a value to the clipboard, shows 'Copied' for a moment and announces it.
Status: stable | Category: buttons | Related: button, icon-button, use-clipboard
Import: import {CopyButton} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value: string — The text written to the clipboard when the button is pressed.
- children?: ReactNode — Visible text. Leave it out for an icon-only button that is named by `label`.
- label?: string = 'Copy' — The accessible name of the icon-only button (the text button is named by its children). Default "Copy".
- copiedLabel?: string = 'Copied' — What is shown (text button) and announced to screen readers after a successful copy. Default "Copied".
- failedLabel?: string = 'Copy failed' — What is announced when the browser refuses to copy. Default "Copy failed".
- timeout?: number — How long the copied state lasts, in milliseconds. Default 2000.
- onCopied?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the copied text after a successful copy.

Usage:
```tsx
import {CopyButton} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', alignItems: 'center'}}>
  <code>npm i @monoline/react</code>
  <CopyButton value="npm i @monoline/react" label="Copy install command" size="sm" />
  <CopyButton value="npm i @monoline/react" variant="solid">Copy command</CopyButton>
</div>
```

A11y:
- Native button; the icon-only form is named by the label prop (default 'Copy').
- The result is announced in a polite role=status region: 'Copied' or 'Copy failed'.
- The text button changes its visible text to the copied label and resets itself.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, btn-icon
Data attributes: data-copied
Source: registry/copy-button.json

## Data grid (data-grid)
A virtualised, keyboard-navigable grid for very large data sets, with sortable columns and row selection.
Status: beta | Category: data-display | Related: empty-state
Import: import {DataGrid} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label?: string
- aria-labelledby?: string
- columns: DataGridColumn<T>[] — The column definitions: id, header, how to read each cell, width and sortability.
- rows: T[] — All the rows. Only the visible ones are rendered, so tens of thousands are fine.
- getRowId?: ((row: T, index: number) => string) — Stable id per row, used for selection. Default: the row's position in `rows`.
- rowHeight?: number = 36 — Row height in px. Every row has the same height; that is what makes virtualising cheap. Default 36.
- height?: string | number = 400 — Height of the scrolling grid, header included. Default 400.
- overscan?: number = 5 — Extra rows rendered above and below the visible ones. Default 5.
- selectionMode?: "none" | "multiple" | "single" = 'none' — Whether rows can be selected: `none` (default), `single` or `multiple`.
- selectedIds?: string[] — Controlled selected row ids. Pair with `onSelectedIdsChange`.
- defaultSelectedIds?: string[] — Initially selected row ids when uncontrolled.
- onSelectedIdsChange?: ((ids: string[]) => void) — Called with the new list of selected row ids.
- sort?: DataGridSort | null — Controlled sort; `null` is unsorted.
- defaultSort?: DataGridSort | null = null — Initial sort when uncontrolled; `null` is unsorted.
- onSortChange?: ((sort: DataGridSort | null) => void) — Called with the new sort, or `null` when sorting is cleared.
- manualSort?: boolean — Do not sort in the grid: `rows` arrive already ordered (server-side sorting).
- emptyState?: ReactNode — Shown when `rows` is empty.

Usage:
```tsx
import {DataGrid, type DataGridColumn} from '@monoline/react';

interface Order { id: string; customer: string; city: string; items: number; total: number }

const cities = ['Pune', 'Berlin', 'Lagos', 'Lima', 'Oslo', 'Hanoi', 'Cairo', 'Quito'];

const make = (count: number): Order[] => Array.from({length: count}, (_, i) => ({
  id: `ORD-${i + 1}`, customer: `Customer ${(i * 7919) % 10007}`, city: cities[i % cities.length]!, items: (i * 13) % 9 + 1, total: ((i * 2654435761) % 100000) / 100,
}));

const columns: DataGridColumn<Order>[] = [
  {id: 'id', header: 'Order', field: 'id', width: 120, sortable: true},
  {id: 'customer', header: 'Customer', field: 'customer', sortable: true},
  {id: 'city', header: 'City', field: 'city', sortable: true},
  {id: 'items', header: 'Items', field: 'items', width: 90, sortable: true, align: 'end'},
  {id: 'total', header: 'Total', cell: (r) => r.total.toFixed(2), sortValue: (r) => r.total, width: 110, sortable: true, align: 'end'},
];

const big = make(100000);

<DataGrid aria-label="Orders, 100,000 rows" columns={columns} rows={big} height={320} getRowId={(r) => r.id} />
```

A11y:
- role="grid" with aria-rowcount, aria-colcount, aria-rowindex and aria-colindex so assistive technology knows the full size although only visible rows are in the DOM.
- Roving tabindex: one Tab stop; arrow keys move between cells, Home and End go to the row ends, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the first and last cell, PageUp and PageDown move a screenful.
- Sortable headers carry aria-sort (ascending, descending, none); Enter or Space on a focused header sorts.
- With selectionMode, rows carry aria-selected and Space or a click toggles the focused row; the grid is aria-multiselectable in multiple mode.
- The header row stays visible while scrolling; an empty grid shows an empty state.

CSS classes: empty, empty-icon, empty-title, empty-description, empty-actions, data-grid, data-grid-head, data-grid-body, data-grid-row, data-grid-body-row, data-grid-cell, data-grid-text, data-grid-th, data-grid-sort, data-grid-empty-row, data-grid-empty
Data attributes: data-state: selected; data-align: end; data-sortable; data-direction: desc
Source: registry/data-grid.json

## Data table (data-table)
A table with sortable columns, row selection and pagination.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: table, checkbox, pagination, empty-state
Import: import {DataTable} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- columns: DataTableColumn<T>[] — The column definitions: each has an `id`, a `header`, and optionally an `accessor`, a `cell` renderer, `sortable` and `align`.
- data: T[] — The rows to show; each row's `id` field (or `getRowId`) must be unique.
- getRowId?: ((row: T, index: number) => string) — Stable id for a row. Defaults to `row.id`, then the index.
- label: string — Names the table for assistive tech.
- sort?: DataTableSort | null — Sort state. Controlled with `sort` + `onSortChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultSort`. `null` means unsorted.
- defaultSort?: DataTableSort | null = null — The initial sort when uncontrolled, as `{id, direction}`. Default `null` (unsorted).
- onSortChange?: ((sort: DataTableSort | null) => void) — Called with the new sort (`null` when sorting is cleared) when the user clicks a sortable header.
- selectable?: boolean — Adds a checkbox column. Selected row ids: controlled with `selection` + `onSelectionChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultSelection`.
- selection?: string[] — Ids of the selected rows when controlled. Pair with `onSelectionChange` and `selectable`.
- defaultSelection?: string[] = [] — Ids of the rows selected at first when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onSelectionChange?: ((ids: string[]) => void) — Called with the full list of selected row ids when the user checks or unchecks a row.
- pageSize?: number — Rows per page. Omit to show every row.
- emptyTitle?: ReactNode = 'No results' — Heading shown when there are no rows. Default "No results".
- emptyDescription?: ReactNode — Optional sentence under the empty heading, for example how to add the first row.

Usage:
```tsx
import {DataTable, type DataTableColumn} from '@monoline/react';

interface Person {id: string; name: string; role: string; projects: number}

const people: Person[] = [
  ['Ada Lovelace', 'Engineer', 4], ['Grace Hopper', 'Admiral', 9], ['Alan Turing', 'Researcher', 6], ['Katherine Johnson', 'Mathematician', 7],
  ['Linus Torvalds', 'Maintainer', 12], ['Margaret Hamilton', 'Director', 5], ['Dennis Ritchie', 'Engineer', 3], ['Barbara Liskov', 'Professor', 8],
].map(([name, role, projects], i) => ({id: String(i), name: name as string, role: role as string, projects: projects as number}));

const columns: DataTableColumn<Person>[] = [
  {id: 'name', header: 'Name', sortable: true},
  {id: 'role', header: 'Role', sortable: true},
  {id: 'projects', header: 'Projects', sortable: true, align: 'end'},
];

<DataTable label="Team" columns={columns} data={people} defaultSort={{id: 'name', direction: 'asc'}} />
```

A11y:
- Native table; sortable headers hold a real button and the th carries aria-sort (ascending, descending, none).
- Each row and the select-all box are checkboxes with names; select-all shows the indeterminate state for a partial selection.
- The count of selected rows is announced through a status region.
- An empty result shows an empty state inside the table; pagination is a nav landmark of buttons.

CSS classes: table-wrap, table, num, checkbox, radio, sw, checkbox-mark, radio-dot, radio-group, sw-thumb, crumbs, pager, steps, step, topbar, brand, topbar-nav, tab, tabpanel, empty, empty-icon, empty-title, empty-description, empty-actions, data-table-sort-btn, data-table-sort, data-table, data-table-check, data-table-footer
Data attributes: data-state: checked | indeterminate | done | selected; data-orientation: horizontal; data-direction: desc
Source: registry/data-table.json

## Date picker (date-picker)
A button that opens a calendar and shows the chosen date.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Primitive: radix-ui/Popover | Related: calendar, popover, field
Import: import {DatePicker} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- placeholder?: string = 'Pick a date' — Text shown on the button while no date is chosen. Default "Pick a date".
- format?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions = {dateStyle: 'medium'} — Intl options for the text on the button. Default: medium date.
- disabled?: boolean — Stops the user opening the calendar.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.
- className?: string — Extra class name for the trigger button.
- aria-label?: string — Names the control when it is not inside a Field.

Usage:
```tsx
import {DatePicker, Field} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '260px', minHeight: '360px'}}><Field label="Due date"><DatePicker weekStartsOn={1} /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- The trigger is a button naming the field and the current value; it opens a dialog with the calendar.
- Choosing a date closes the dialog and returns focus to the trigger; Escape closes without changing.
- All calendar keyboard behaviour applies inside.
- With `clearable`, a "Clear date" button in the popover removes the date, closes it and returns focus to the trigger.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, calendar, calendar-head, calendar-title, calendar-nav, calendar-grid, calendar-day, date-trigger, date-popover

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):

- className?: string — Extra class name for the trigger button.

```tsx
import {DateRangePicker, Field} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px', minHeight: '440px'}}><Field label="Stay"><DateRangePicker weekStartsOn={1} /></Field></div>
```

## Dialog (dialog)
A modal window for a question or short task that blocks the page.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/Dialog | Related: alert-dialog, command, context-menu
Import: import {Dialog} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- showClose?: boolean = true — Shows a "Close" text button in the corner. Escape and the overlay always close it.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Dialog, DialogClose, DialogContent, DialogDescription, DialogFooter, DialogHeader, DialogTitle, DialogTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger asChild><Button>Overwrite copy</Button></DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader><DialogTitle>Overwrite the remote copy?</DialogTitle><DialogDescription>The copy on this device is newer. Changes from 12 March on the other device will be lost.</DialogDescription></DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter><DialogClose asChild><Button>Keep both</Button></DialogClose><DialogClose asChild><Button variant="solid">Overwrite</Button></DialogClose></DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>
```

A11y:
- role=dialog with aria-modal; the title names it and the description describes it.
- Focus moves into the dialog, is trapped there, and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape and the Close button close it; the page behind is inert.

CSS classes: dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title
Source: registry/dialog.json

## Direction provider (direction-provider)
Sets the reading direction (ltr or rtl) once for every Radix-based component below it.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Primitive: radix-ui/Direction | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {DirectionProvider} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- dir: "ltr" | "rtl" — Reading direction for everything below: `ltr` or `rtl`.
- children?: ReactNode — The part of the app that should use this direction.

Usage:
```tsx
import {DirectionProvider, Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<div dir="rtl"><DirectionProvider dir="rtl"><Tabs defaultValue="a"><TabsList aria-label="Sections"><TabsTrigger value="a">الأول</TabsTrigger><TabsTrigger value="b">الثاني</TabsTrigger></TabsList><TabsContent value="a">محتوى</TabsContent><TabsContent value="b">محتوى آخر</TabsContent></Tabs></DirectionProvider></div>
```

A11y:
- Arrow keys follow the reading direction: in rtl, ArrowLeft moves to the next tab, slider step up or toolbar item.
- Pair it with a dir attribute on html so the stylesheet mirrors layout too.
Source: registry/direction-provider.json

## Dot pattern (dot-pattern)

```tsx
import {DotPattern} from '@monoline/react';
```

## Drawer (drawer)
A panel that slides in from an edge for secondary tasks, details or navigation.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/Dialog | Related: alert-dialog, command, context-menu
Import: import {Drawer} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- side?: "start" | "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" | "end" = 'right' — The edge it slides from. `start` and `end` follow the reading direction; `left` and `right` are fixed.
- showClose?: boolean = true — Shows a "Close" text button. Escape and the overlay always close it.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Drawer, DrawerContent, DrawerDescription, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}>
  {(['right', 'left'] as const).map((side) => (
    <Drawer key={side}>
      <DrawerTrigger asChild><Button>Open {side}</Button></DrawerTrigger>
      <DrawerContent side={side}><DrawerHeader><DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle><DrawerDescription>Narrow the list by status or owner.</DrawerDescription></DrawerHeader></DrawerContent>
    </Drawer>
  ))}
</div>
```

A11y:
- role="dialog" named by the title.
- Focus is trapped while open and returns to the trigger on close.
- Escape and the overlay close it.

CSS classes: dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title, drawer-content
Data attributes: data-side: right | end | left | start | top | bottom
Source: registry/drawer.json

```tsx
import {Button, DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuLabel, DropdownMenuSeparator, DropdownMenuTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<DropdownMenu>

    <DropdownMenuItem>Duplicate</DropdownMenuItem>

    <DropdownMenuItem tone="danger">Delete</DropdownMenuItem>
```

A11y:
- role=menu with menuitem, menuitemcheckbox and menuitemradio items.
- Arrow keys move, Enter and Space activate, Escape closes and returns focus, type-ahead jumps to an item.
- The trigger has aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

CSS classes: popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, dropdown, menu, menu-end, danger, menu-sep

## Field (field)
Connects a label, a control, a hint and an error with the right ids and ARIA.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: label
Import: import {Field} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- label: ReactNode — The visible label of the control. Required so every control has a name.
- hint?: ReactNode — Help text shown under the control.
- error?: ReactNode — Error message. Its presence marks the control invalid and it is announced politely. Inside a `Form` with `errors`, leave it out and set `name` instead.
- name?: string — The `name` of the control. Inside a `Form` that has `errors`, the Field shows the message for this name, so you pass each error once.
- required?: boolean = false — Marks the control as required: adds a required marker to the label and sets `required` on the control. Default false.
- children: ReactNode — The control: Input, Textarea, Select trigger, etc.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, Input} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: 360}}><Field label="Email" hint="We never share it." required><Input type="email" placeholder="you@example.com" /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- The label is bound to the control by id, so it has an accessible name.
- Hint and error are linked with aria-describedby; an error sets aria-invalid and is announced via role=alert.
- required sets the native required attribute on the control.
- Inside a Form with errors, a Field with a matching name shows that error once; the form summary announces it, so the inline text is not a second alert.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, field-error, field-ok, input-group, input-affix, field-required, form-row
Data attributes: data-valid: true
Source: registry/field.json

## Fieldset (fieldset)
Group related controls under one legend.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {Fieldset} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- legend: ReactNode — The group's name. Required so the fieldset always has an accessible name.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, Fieldset, Input} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '360px'}}><Fieldset legend="Contact"><Field label="Name"><Input /></Field><Field label="Email"><Input type="email" /></Field></Fieldset></div>
```

A11y:
- Native fieldset and legend: screen readers announce the legend with each control.
- disabled on the fieldset disables every control inside.

CSS classes: fieldset, fieldset-legend
Source: registry/fieldset.json

## File upload (file-upload)
Choose files by browsing or dropping them, and see what is selected.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {FileUpload} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- label?: ReactNode = 'Drop files here or choose' — The visible prompt, for example "Drop files here or choose".
- onFilesChange?: ((files: File[]) => void) — Called with the full current list whenever it changes.

Usage:
```tsx
import {FileUpload} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '420px'}}><FileUpload multiple accept="image/*,.pdf" label="Drop files here or choose" /></div>
```

A11y:
- A native file input stays focusable and operable by keyboard; the drop zone is a label for it.

- Dragging is an extra, never the only way.

CSS classes: upload, upload-zone, upload-list, upload-name, upload-remove, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block
Data attributes: data-over
Source: registry/file-upload.json

## Flex (flex)
A flex container with direction, wrap, align, justify, gap and an inline form. Stack covers the common case.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {Flex} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- direction?: "row" | "column" | "row-reverse" | "column-reverse" = 'row' — Main axis: `row` (default), `column`, `row-reverse` or `column-reverse`.
- wrap?: boolean — Lets children wrap onto new lines instead of shrinking. Default false.
- align?: "center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" | "baseline" — Cross-axis alignment (`align-items`): `start`, `center`, `end`, `stretch` or `baseline`.
- justify?: "center" | "start" | "end" | "between" | "around" — Main-axis distribution (`justify-content`): `start`, `center`, `end`, `between` or `around`.
- gap?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 — Step on the spacing scale: 1 = --s1 up to 9.
- inline?: boolean — `inline-flex` instead of `flex`.
- asChild?: boolean — Render the child element (a `ul`, `nav`, `section`) with the flex styles instead of a `div`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Badge, Flex} from '@monoline/react';

<Flex justify="between" align="center" gap={3}><Badge>left</Badge><Badge>right</Badge></Flex>
```

A11y:
- A plain element; adds no roles. Reversed directions change visual order only, so keep the source order meaningful.

CSS classes: flex, flex-inline, flex-wrap
Data attributes: data-direction: column | row-reverse | column-reverse; data-align: start | center | end | stretch | baseline; data-justify: start | center | end | between | around
Source: registry/flex.json

## Form (form)
A form wrapper with a submit helper, an error summary that links to invalid fields, and an actions footer.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: field, button
Import: import {Form} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- onSubmit?: ((event: FormEvent<HTMLFormElement>) => void) — Called with the submit event. Combine with `preventDefault` when you handle the form in JS.
- preventDefault?: boolean — Call `event.preventDefault()` before `onSubmit`, for forms handled in JS. Off by default so native posts still work.
- errors?: FormError[] — Errors to list in a summary at the top of the form. Give each `Field` the same `name` and it shows its own message, so you pass each error once. A Field's own `error` prop still wins.
- errorsTitle?: ReactNode = 'Fix these to continue' — Heading of the summary. Default "Fix these to continue".

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, Field, Form, FormActions, Input, type FormError} from '@monoline/react';

function Example() {
  const [errors, setErrors] = useState<FormError[]>([]);
  return (
    <Form
      aria-label="Contact"
      noValidate
      preventDefault
      errors={errors}
      onSubmit={(e) => {
        const data = new FormData(e.currentTarget);
        const next: FormError[] = [];
        if (!data.get('name')) next.push({name: 'name', message: 'Enter your name.'});
        if (!data.get('email')) next.push({name: 'email', message: 'Enter your email.'});
        setErrors(next);
      }}
    >
      <Field label="Name" name="name"><Input name="name" /></Field>
      <Field label="Email" name="email"><Input name="email" type="email" /></Field>
      <FormActions><Button type="submit" variant="solid">Send</Button><Button type="reset">Clear</Button></FormActions>
    </Form>
  );
}

<Example />
```

A11y:
- A native form; give it an accessible name with aria-label or aria-labelledby when the page has several.
- The error summary is a role=alert region at the top; each item is a link that moves focus to the invalid control.
- Pass each error once, in the Form's errors; a Field with the same name shows it inline and sets aria-invalid and aria-describedby on its control. The summary announces it, so the inline text is not announced twice.

CSS classes: form, form-errors, form-errors-title, form-actions
Source: registry/form.json

## Grid (grid)
A responsive grid of equal columns with one gap.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {Grid} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- columns?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 — Fixed number of equal columns. Omit for an auto-fit grid.
- minColumn?: string = '16rem' — With auto-fit: the smallest a column may be, as a CSS length such as `16rem`.
- gap?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 = 4 — Step on the spacing scale, 1 to 9.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Card, Grid} from '@monoline/react';

<Grid columns={3}>{['One', 'Two', 'Three'].map((n) => <Card key={n}>{n}</Card>)}</Grid>
```

A11y:
- A plain div; source order is reading order.

CSS classes: grid, grid-fixed
Source: registry/grid.json
