## Heading (heading)
A heading whose level (for structure) is separate from its size (for looks).
Status: stable | Category: typography | Related: kbd, link, text
Import: import {Heading} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- level?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 2 — Document outline level, 1 to 6.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "display" | "xl" — Look. Defaults follow the level. `display` uses the display font.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Heading} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}><Heading level={1}>Display</Heading><Heading level={2}>Section</Heading><Heading level={3}>Subsection</Heading><Heading level={2} size="sm">An h2 that looks small</Heading></div>
```

A11y:
- Renders a real h1 to h6; choose the level for the outline, not the size.

CSS classes: heading, heading-display, heading-xl, heading-lg, heading-md, heading-sm

## Icon button (icon-button)

```tsx
<div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}><IconButton aria-label="Add"><Plus /></IconButton><IconButton variant="solid" aria-label="Add item"><Plus /></IconButton><IconButton variant="ghost" size="sm" aria-label="Add row"><Plus /></IconButton></div>
```

## Image (image)
An image with required alt text, a ratio, and a fallback when it fails to load.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Image} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- alt: string — Required. Describe the image, or pass "" if it is decorative.
- ratio?: number — Width / height, for example `16 / 9`. Reserves space so the page does not jump.
- fit?: "cover" | "contain" = 'cover' — How the image fills its box when `ratio` crops it: `cover` (default) or `contain`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Image} from '@monoline/react';

const svg = (c: string) => 'data:image/svg+xml;utf8,' + encodeURIComponent(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="320" height="180"><rect width="320" height="180" fill="${c}"/></svg>`);

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px'}}><Image src={svg('#999')} alt="A grey placeholder" ratio={16 / 9} /></div>
```

A11y:
- alt is required; use alt="" only for purely decorative images.
- The fallback shows the alt text so the content is not lost when loading fails.

CSS classes: image, image-cover, image-contain, image-fallback
Source: registry/image.json

## Image gallery (image-gallery)
A thumbnail grid that opens a lightbox with previous and next.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: button, dialog
Import: import {ImageGallery} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- images: GalleryImage[] — The images, in order. Each needs `alt` text.
- columns?: number = 3 — Number of columns in the thumbnail grid. Default 3.
- onIndexChange?: ((index: number) => void) — Called with the index of the image shown whenever the lightbox opens or moves.

Usage:
```tsx
import {ImageGallery, type GalleryImage} from '@monoline/react';

const tile = (n: number, fill: string) => `data:image/svg+xml;utf8,${encodeURIComponent(`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300"><rect width="400" height="300" fill="${fill}"/><text x="200" y="165" font-family="monospace" font-size="64" text-anchor="middle" fill="#fff">${n}</text></svg>`)}`;

const images: GalleryImage[] = ['#6b4f3a', '#3a5a6b', '#4f6b3a', '#6b3a5a', '#5a3a6b', '#3a6b5a'].map((c, i) => ({src: tile(i + 1, c), alt: `Sample picture ${i + 1}, a flat colour with its number`, caption: `Picture ${i + 1}`}));

<div style={{maxWidth: '480px'}}><ImageGallery images={images} /></div>
```

A11y:
- Each thumbnail is a button named by the image's required alt text, with aria-haspopup=dialog.
- The lightbox is a modal dialog titled 'Image 2 of 5'; focus moves in, is trapped, and returns to the thumbnail on close.
- ArrowLeft and ArrowRight (swapped in RTL) and the Previous and Next buttons move through the images and wrap; a horizontal swipe does the same; Escape closes.
- A polite status message announces the new image's alt text and position. Neighbouring images are preloaded.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, dialog-overlay, dialog-content, dialog-header, dialog-footer, dialog-description, dialog-close, dialog-title, image-gallery, image-gallery-thumb, image-gallery-lightbox, image-gallery-title, image-gallery-figure, image-gallery-nav
Source: registry/image-gallery.json

## Line chart (line-chart)
Show how one or more values change across an ordered axis, with straight or stepped lines.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {LineChart} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- showPoints?: boolean — Mark each data point. A single point is always marked.

Usage:
```tsx
import {LineChart} from '@monoline/react';

<LineChart title="Response time" showPoints data={[{label: 'Mon', value: 120}, {label: 'Tue', value: 98}, {label: 'Wed', value: 143}, {label: 'Thu', value: 110}, {label: 'Fri', value: 87}]} />
```

A11y:
- The chart is role=img with the required title as its name.
- A visually hidden table lists every value, one row per category, for screen readers.
- One focusable stop per category with a spoken label; Arrow keys move between them and Escape hides the tooltip.
- The value tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus.
- Series differ by dash pattern and marker shape as well as colour, and the legend names them.
- No entrance animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: chart, chart-plot, chart-svg, chart-hits, chart-s0, chart-s1, chart-s2, chart-s3, chart-s4, chart-tick, chart-value, chart-rule, chart-zero, chart-outline, chart-pat, chart-pat-dot, chart-line, chart-area, chart-hit, chart-tip, chart-tip-title, chart-tip-row, chart-tip-value, chart-legend, chart-legend-detail, chart-swatch, chart-empty, chart-marks, chart-point, chart-guide

## Marquee (marquee)
Scroll a row of items endlessly; pauses on hover and stops for reduced motion.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {Marquee} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- duration?: number = 30 — Seconds for one full loop.
- reverse?: boolean — Scroll to the right instead of the left. Default false.
- pauseOnHover?: boolean = true — Stop when the pointer is over it or focus is inside. Default true.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Marquee} from '@monoline/react';

<Marquee duration={20}>{['Acme', 'Globex', 'Initech', 'Umbrella', 'Hooli'].map((n) => <span key={n} style={{padding: '0 var(--s5)', fontFamily: 'var(--font-display)'}}>{n}</span>)}</Marquee>
```

A11y:
- The duplicate copy is aria-hidden so screen readers read the items once.
- Pauses on hover and focus; animation is off under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: marquee, marquee-track, marquee-reverse, marquee-pause
Source: registry/marquee.json

## Mentions (mentions)
A textarea that suggests people when you type @.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {Mentions} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: string — The text when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string = '' — The initial text when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the full text after every edit and after a mention is inserted.
- options?: MentionOption[] = [] — The choices, filtered by what is typed after the trigger. Use `onSearch` instead to load them.
- onSearch?: ((query: string, trigger: string) => MentionOption[] | Promise<MentionOption[]>) — Loads choices for the typed query, for example from a server. Return the options or a promise of them. Late answers for an older query are ignored. Replaces `options` filtering when given.
- triggers?: string[] = ['@'] — Characters that open the list when typed at the start of a word. Default `["@"]`.
- onMentionSelect?: ((option: MentionOption, trigger: string) => void) — Called with the option and the trigger when the user inserts a mention.
- loadingText?: string = 'Loading' — Text shown while `onSearch` is loading. Default "Loading".
- emptyText?: string = 'No matches' — Text shown when nothing matches. Default "No matches".
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, Mentions, type MentionOption} from '@monoline/react';

const people: MentionOption[] = [
  {value: 'ada', label: 'Ada Lovelace'},
  {value: 'grace', label: 'Grace Hopper'},
  {value: 'alan', label: 'Alan Turing'},
  {value: 'linus', label: 'Linus Torvalds', disabled: true},
];

<div style={{maxWidth: '360px', minHeight: '220px'}}><Field label="Comment"><Mentions options={people} rows={3} /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- The textarea keeps its native textbox role (ARIA does not allow combobox on a textarea) and adds aria-haspopup="listbox", aria-autocomplete="list", aria-controls while the list is open and aria-activedescendant for the highlighted option; the list is a listbox of options.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp move the highlight, Enter or Tab insert the mention, Escape closes the list without inserting; focus never leaves the textarea.
- A polite status region announces how many suggestions there are, and when they are loading or empty.
- Async loading ignores answers for outdated queries so the list never shows stale results.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, mentions, mentions-list, mentions-option, mentions-note
Data attributes: data-active
Source: registry/mentions.json

## Menubar (menubar)
A horizontal bar of menus, like File, Edit and View in a desktop app.

Import: import {Menubar} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- tone?: "danger" | "default" = 'default' — `danger` highlights in the danger colour.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarSeparator, MenubarTrigger} from '@monoline/react';

<Menubar aria-label="Application">
  <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>New file</MenubarItem><MenubarItem>Open</MenubarItem><MenubarSeparator /><MenubarItem>Quit</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
  <MenubarMenu><MenubarTrigger>Edit</MenubarTrigger><MenubarContent><MenubarItem>Undo</MenubarItem><MenubarItem>Redo</MenubarItem></MenubarContent></MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>
```

A11y:
- role="menubar"; arrow keys move between menus and items, Enter or Space opens.
- Escape closes the open menu and returns focus to its trigger.

CSS classes: popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, dropdown, menu, menu-end, danger, menu-sep, menubar, menubar-trigger
Data attributes: data-highlighted; data-disabled; data-variant: danger; data-state: open
Source: registry/menubar.json

## Multi select (multi-select)
Type to filter a list and pick several options, shown as removable tags.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: field, tag
Import: import {MultiSelect} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- options: MultiSelectOption[] — The choices, each with a `value`, a `label` and an optional `disabled`. The user filters them by typing part of the label.
- value?: string[] — The chosen option values when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string[] = [] — The initially chosen option values when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string[]) => void) — Called with the full list of chosen values.
- emptyText?: string = 'No matches' — Shown when nothing matches.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, MultiSelect} from '@monoline/react';

const options = ['Ada Lovelace', 'Grace Hopper', 'Alan Turing', 'Katherine Johnson', 'Linus Torvalds'].map((n) => ({value: n.toLowerCase().replace(/\W+/g, '-'), label: n}));

<div style={{maxWidth: '360px', minHeight: '280px'}}><Field label="People"><MultiSelect options={options} placeholder="Type a name" defaultValue={['ada-lovelace']} /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- ARIA 1.2 combobox with a listbox that has aria-multiselectable; options carry aria-selected.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp move, Enter toggles the active option, Escape closes, Tab leaves.
- Backspace in an empty field removes the last tag; each tag has a button named "Remove <label>".

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, avatar, avatar-sm, avatar-lg, avatar-line, avatar-group, tag, stat, stat-value, stat-note, multi-select, multi-select-box, multi-select-input, multi-select-list, multi-select-option, multi-select-empty
Data attributes: data-invalid; data-disabled; data-active; data-size: sm | lg
Source: registry/multi-select.json

## Native select (native-select)
The browser select, styled. Best on mobile and for long simple lists.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: field
Import: import {NativeSelect} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button and the other form controls at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the control invalid (`aria-invalid`). A surrounding Field sets this from its `error`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, NativeSelect} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '280px'}}><Field label="Plan"><NativeSelect defaultValue="pro"><option value="free">Free</option><option value="pro">Pro</option><option value="team">Team</option></NativeSelect></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- A real select element: native keyboard, typeahead and mobile pickers.
- Inside a Field it is labelled and described automatically.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt
Source: registry/native-select.json

## Notification center (notification-center)
A bell button with an unread count that opens a list of notifications, with mark read, clear and an empty state.
Status: stable | Category: feedback | Related: button, icon-button, popover
Import: import {NotificationCenter} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- notifications: NotificationItem[] — The notifications, newest first. You own this list: update it in the callbacks below.
- onMarkRead?: ((id: string) => void) — Called with the id when the user marks one notification as read. Hides that item's "Mark read" button once `read` is true.
- onMarkAllRead?: (() => void) — Called when the user chooses "Mark all read". The button is disabled when nothing is unread.
- onClear?: (() => void) — Called when the user chooses "Clear all". The button is disabled when the list is empty.
- label?: string = 'Notifications' — Name of the bell button and the panel. Default "Notifications".
- emptyText?: string = "You're all caught up." — Shown when there are no notifications. Default "You're all caught up."

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {NotificationCenter, type NotificationItem} from '@monoline/react';

const start: NotificationItem[] = [
  {id: '1', title: 'Deploy finished', description: 'Production, 41 seconds.', time: '2 min ago'},
  {id: '2', title: 'Ada commented on your pull request', time: '1 hour ago'},
  {id: '3', title: 'Invoice paid', time: 'Yesterday', read: true},
];

function Demo1() {
  const [list, setList] = useState(start);
  return (
    <div style={{display: 'flex', justifyContent: 'flex-end', minHeight: '280px'}}>
      <NotificationCenter
        notifications={list}
        onMarkRead={(id) => setList((l) => l.map((n) => (n.id === id ? {...n, read: true} : n)))}
        onMarkAllRead={() => setList((l) => l.map((n) => ({...n, read: true})))}
        onClear={() => setList([])}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

<Demo1 />
```

A11y:
- The bell is a button named 'Notifications, 3 unread'; the visible count badge is aria-hidden so the number is announced once.
- The panel is a labelled dialog: Escape or an outside click closes it and focus returns to the bell.
- Unread items are bold, start with a visually hidden 'Unread:' and have a 'Mark read' button named after the item; unread is never shown by colour alone.
- 'Mark all read' and 'Clear all' are disabled when they have nothing to do; an empty list shows plain text.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, swatch, check, check-pass, check-fail, badge, badge-solid, badge-accent, kbd, key-hints, dot, heat-0, heat-1, heat-2, heat-3, heat-4, btn-icon, popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, notification-center, notification-center-badge, notification-center-panel, notification-center-head, notification-center-actions, notification-center-list, notification-center-item, notification-center-text, notification-center-title, notification-center-desc, notification-center-time, notification-center-empty
Data attributes: data-highlighted; data-disabled; data-variant: danger; data-unread
Source: registry/notification-center.json

## Number ticker (number-ticker)
Count up to a number when it scrolls into view. Shows the final value at once for reduced motion.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {NumberTicker} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value: number — The number to count to. Screen readers get this, never the frames in between.
- from?: number = 0 — Where the count starts. Default 0.
- duration?: number = 1500 — Milliseconds for the count. Default 1500.
- decimals?: number = 0 — Digits after the decimal point. Default 0.
- format?: ((n: number) => string) — Custom formatting, for currency or units. Overrides `decimals`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {NumberTicker} from '@monoline/react';

<p style={{fontFamily: 'var(--font-display)', fontSize: 'var(--display-sm)'}}><NumberTicker value={12840} /></p>
```

A11y:
- Screen readers get the final number from an sr-only copy; the animated frames are aria-hidden.
- With prefers-reduced-motion the final number shows immediately and nothing animates.

CSS classes: number-ticker
Source: registry/number-ticker.json

## Orbiting circles (orbiting-circles)
Small items circling a centre. Decorative.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {OrbitingCircles} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- radius?: number = 96 — Orbit radius in px. Default 96.
- duration?: number = 20 — Seconds for one full turn. Default 20.
- reverse?: boolean — Turn the other way.
- ring?: boolean = true — Draw the orbit as a thin ring. Default true.
- center?: ReactNode — Fixed content in the centre.

Usage:
```tsx
import {OrbitingCircles} from '@monoline/react';

const dot = (t: string) => <span style={{display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center', width: 'var(--s7)', height: 'var(--s7)', border: '1px solid var(--foreground)', background: 'var(--background)', fontSize: 'var(--text-xs)'}}>{t}</span>;

<div style={{display: 'grid', placeItems: 'center'}}>
  <OrbitingCircles radius={96} center={dot('M')}>{dot('A')}{dot('B')}{dot('C')}</OrbitingCircles>
</div>
```

A11y:
- Decorative: the whole element is aria-hidden, so nothing inside it is read or reachable by assistive tech.
- Under prefers-reduced-motion the items stop, evenly spaced around the ring.

CSS classes: orbit, orbit-ring, orbit-center, orbit-item, orbit-reverse
Source: registry/orbiting-circles.json

## OTP input (otp-input)
Enter a one-time code, one digit per box, with paste support.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {OtpInput} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label: string — Names the group, for example "Verification code".
- length?: number = 6 — Number of boxes, which is the length of the code. Default 6.
- value?: string — The code typed so far when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string = '' — The code typed at first when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the whole code (so far) every time a character is added or removed.
- onComplete?: ((value: string) => void) — Called once when every box is filled.
- alphanumeric?: boolean — Allow letters as well as digits.
- disabled?: boolean — Disables every box.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the boxes as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {OtpInput} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [done, setDone] = useState('');
  return <div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}><OtpInput aria-label="Verification code" onComplete={setDone} /><p className="muted small" role="status">{done ? `Entered ${done}` : 'Enter 6 digits'}</p></div>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- The boxes are a group with a name; each box is labelled "Digit N of M".
- Typing moves forward, Backspace moves back, arrows move, pasting fills all boxes.
- inputmode="numeric" and autocomplete="one-time-code" for mobile and autofill.

CSS classes: otp, otp-box
Source: registry/otp-input.json

## Overflow list (overflow-list)
A row of items that shows as many as fit and puts the rest in a '+N' menu.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: button, dropdown-menu
Import: import {OverflowList} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- items: OverflowItem[] — The items in order. As many as fit are shown; the rest move into a "+N" menu.
- moreLabel?: ((hidden: number) => string) = (n) => `${n} more ${n === 1 ? 'item' : 'items'}` — Accessible name of the "+N" button, given the number of hidden items. Default "N more items".

Usage:
```tsx
import {OverflowList, Tag} from '@monoline/react';

const names = ['Design', 'Engineering', 'Marketing', 'Support', 'Finance', 'Legal', 'People', 'Research'];

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px', resize: 'horizontal', overflow: 'auto', paddingBlock: 'var(--s2)'}}>
  <OverflowList items={names.map((n) => ({id: n, label: <Tag>{n}</Tag>}))} />
</div>
```

A11y:
- Items that do not fit are visibility:hidden, so they are neither focusable nor read out; the same items are reachable in the menu.
- The '+N' button is named '3 more items' (customisable with moreLabel) and opens a menu: Enter, Space or ArrowDown opens, arrows move, Escape closes and returns focus to the button.
- Layout is recalculated by a ResizeObserver when the container or the items change.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, dropdown, menu, menu-end, menu-item, danger, menu-sep, overflow-list, overflow-list-items, overflow-list-item, overflow-list-more
Data attributes: data-hidden
Source: registry/overflow-list.json

## Pagination (pagination)

Import: import {Pagination} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):

- defaultPage?: number = 1 — The starting page when uncontrolled. Default 1.
- pageCount: number — Total number of pages.
- onPageChange?: ((page: number) => void) — Called with the new 1-based page number when the user picks a page or presses Prev or Next.
- siblings?: number = 1 — How many numbers to show on each side of the current page.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Pagination} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo1() {

  return <Pagination page={page} pageCount={20} onPageChange={setPage} />;
}

<Demo1 />
```

A11y:
- A nav landmark; each page is a button named "Page N" and the current one has aria-current=page.
- Prev and Next are disabled at the ends.
- The gap marker is hidden from assistive tech.

CSS classes: crumbs, pager, steps, step, topbar, brand, topbar-nav, tab, tabpanel
Data attributes: data-state: done
Source: registry/pagination.json

## Pie chart (pie-chart)
Parts of a whole as a pie, or a donut with innerRadius.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {PieChart} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: string — Accessible name and table caption. Required.
- data: ChartDatum[] — Slices: `[{label: 'Search', value: 40}]`. Negative values count as 0.
- innerRadius?: number = 0 — Hole size as a fraction of the radius, from 0 (pie) to just under 1. 0.6 makes a donut. Default 0.
- height?: number = 240 — Chart height in px. Default 240.
- valueFormat?: ((value: number) => string) — Format a value for the legend, tooltip and table.

Usage:
```tsx
import {PieChart} from '@monoline/react';

const sources = [{label: 'Search', value: 46}, {label: 'Direct', value: 28}, {label: 'Email', value: 14}, {label: 'Referral', value: 8}, {label: 'Social', value: 4}];

<PieChart title="Traffic by source" data={sources} />
```

A11y:
- The chart is role=img with the required title as its name.
- A visually hidden table lists every slice with its value and share.
- One focusable stop per slice with a spoken label; Arrow keys move between them and Escape hides the tooltip.
- The value tooltip opens on hover and on keyboard focus.
- Slices differ by fill pattern as well as colour, and the legend lists each with its value and share.
- No entrance animation under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: chart, chart-plot, chart-svg, chart-hits, chart-s0, chart-s1, chart-s2, chart-s3, chart-s4, chart-tick, chart-value, chart-rule, chart-zero, chart-outline, chart-pat, chart-pat-dot, chart-line, chart-area, chart-hit, chart-tip, chart-tip-title, chart-tip-row, chart-tip-value, chart-legend, chart-legend-detail, chart-swatch, chart-empty, chart-marks, chart-slice
Data attributes: data-active; data-align: start | end
Source: registry/pie-chart.json

## Range calendar (range-calendar)
A month grid for picking a start and an end date.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {RangeCalendar} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: DateRange — The selected range when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: DateRange = EMPTY — The initially selected range when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((range: DateRange) => void) — Called after every pick. The first pick gives `{start, end: null}`; the second completes the range.
- weekStartsOn?: 0 | 1 = 0 — First day of the week: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday. Default 0.
- min?: Date — Earliest selectable date; earlier days are disabled.
- max?: Date — Latest selectable date; later days are disabled.
- isDateDisabled?: ((date: Date) => boolean) — Return true for a day that cannot be picked, such as a holiday.
- locale?: string — BCP 47 locale for month and day names.

Usage:
```tsx
import {RangeCalendar} from '@monoline/react';

<RangeCalendar weekStartsOn={1} />
```

A11y:
- role="grid" with column headers; one day is in the tab order (roving tabindex).
- Enter or Space on a day sets the start, then the end; Escape while picking clears the start.
- Arrow keys move by day and week, Home/End to the start and end of the week, PageUp/PageDown by month; arrows are mirrored in right-to-left.
- The days between start and focus are previewed while picking, by hover and by keyboard.
- Each day button has a full date name; start and end have aria-pressed; a status region announces the chosen range.
- Disabled days (min, max, isDateDisabled) are real disabled buttons.

CSS classes: calendar, calendar-head, calendar-title, calendar-nav, calendar-grid, calendar-day, range-cell, range-calendar
Data attributes: data-outside; data-today; data-in-range; data-range-start; data-preview
Source: registry/range-calendar.json

## Rating (rating)
Pick or show a score from 1 to a maximum, as stars.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {Rating} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label: string — Names the control, for example "Rate this article".
- value?: number — The current score (0 to `max`) when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: number = 0 — The initial score when uncontrolled. Default 0.
- onValueChange?: ((value: number) => void) — Called with the new score (1 to `max`) when the user picks a star.
- max?: number = 5 — Number of stars. Default 5.
- readOnly?: boolean — Shows the score without letting anyone change it.
- name?: string — Name of the underlying radio inputs, so the score submits with a native form. A unique name is generated if omitted.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Rating} from '@monoline/react';

<Rating aria-label="Rate this page" defaultValue={3} />
```

A11y:
- Editable: a radio group (native radios) with arrow-key selection; each star is named "N of M".
- Read-only: role="img" with a text label such as "4 out of 5".

CSS classes: rating, rating-star
Data attributes: data-on
Source: registry/rating.json

## Resizable (resizable)
Panels separated by handles you drag or move with the keyboard.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {ResizablePanelGroup} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
ResizablePanelGroupProps:
- direction?: "vertical" | "horizontal" = 'horizontal' — `horizontal` puts panels side by side; `vertical` stacks them. Default `horizontal`.
- step?: number = 5 — Percent a panel grows or shrinks per arrow-key press (PageUp/PageDown use double). Default 5.
- onLayoutChange?: ((sizes: number[]) => void) — Called with every panel's size in percent (they add up to 100) after each resize.
- children: ReactNode — `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` elements, alternating, as direct children: panel, handle, panel...
ResizablePanelProps:
- defaultSize?: number — Starting size in percent. Panels without one share what is left equally.
- minSize?: number — Smallest size in percent. Default 10.
- maxSize?: number — Largest size in percent. Default 100.
ResizableHandleProps:
- aria-label?: string — Names the handle for screen readers. Default "Resize panels".

Usage:
```tsx
import {ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel, ResizablePanelGroup} from '@monoline/react';

const box = {padding: 'var(--s4)', fontSize: 'var(--text-sm)'};

<ResizablePanelGroup style={{height: '200px', border: '1px solid var(--rule)'}}>
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize={30} minSize={15}><div style={box}>Sidebar</div></ResizablePanel>
  <ResizableHandle aria-label="Resize sidebar" />
  <ResizablePanel defaultSize={70}><div style={box}>Content</div></ResizablePanel>
</ResizablePanelGroup>
```

A11y:
- Each handle is a focusable role="separator" with aria-orientation, aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-controls pointing at the panel it resizes.
- Arrow keys resize by the step (horizontal groups use Left/Right, vertical groups Up/Down; mirrored in right-to-left); PageUp/PageDown resize by double; Home and End jump to the limits.
- minSize and maxSize are enforced for both keyboard and pointer, and are reflected in aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax.
- Handles are at least 24 CSS px to grab and show the focus ring.

CSS classes: resizable, resizable-panel, resizable-handle
Data attributes: data-direction: vertical | horizontal; data-dragging
Source: registry/resizable.json

## Rich text editor (rich-text-editor)
A dependency-free rich text editor with a formatting toolbar and sanitized HTML in and out.
Status: beta | Category: forms | Related: toolbar, popover, button, input
Import: import {RichTextEditor} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label?: string
- aria-labelledby?: string
- value?: string — Controlled content as an HTML string. It is sanitized with `sanitizeHtml` before it is shown.
- defaultValue?: string — Initial HTML when uncontrolled. Sanitized with `sanitizeHtml` before it is shown.
- onValueChange?: ((html: string) => void) — Called with sanitized HTML after every edit.
- placeholder?: string — Shown while the editor is empty (a data attribute and CSS, not a text node).
- disabled?: boolean — Disables editing and the toolbar.
- readOnly?: boolean — Shows the content without letting anyone change it; the toolbar is disabled.
- toolbarLabel?: string = 'Text formatting' — Names the formatting toolbar.

Usage:
```tsx
import {RichTextEditor} from '@monoline/react';

<RichTextEditor aria-label="Notes" placeholder="Write something…" />
```

A11y:
- The editing region has role="textbox", aria-multiline and an accessible name; the toolbar is a named toolbar with one tab stop and arrow-key movement.
- Toggle buttons (bold, italic, underline, lists, headings, quote) carry aria-pressed that follows the selection.
- Cmd/Ctrl+B, I, U and K apply bold, italic, underline and open the link prompt; Escape in the toolbar returns focus to the editor.
- The link prompt is a labelled popover; an invalid address is announced as an alert and links are limited to http, https and mailto.
- Pasted content is sanitized to a small tag allowlist; disabled and read-only set aria-disabled and aria-readonly and turn the toolbar off.

CSS classes: toolbar, toolbar-item, toolbar-sep, popover, menu-content, menu-item, menu-label, menu-indicator, menu-item-check, btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, field-error, field-ok, input-group, input-affix, field-required, form-row, rte, rte-toolbar, rte-content, rte-link, rte-link-label, rte-link-error, rte-link-actions
Data attributes: data-state: on; data-highlighted; data-disabled; data-variant: danger; data-valid: true; data-empty; data-readonly
Source: registry/rich-text-editor.json

## Rolling number (rolling-number)
A number whose digits roll to the new value when it changes. Screen readers read the final value.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {RollingNumber} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value: number — The number to show. When it changes, each digit rolls to its new value.
- locale?: string — BCP 47 locale for the digits and separators, such as "de-DE". Default the browser's locale.
- format?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions — `Intl.NumberFormat` options, for example `{style: 'currency', currency: 'USD'}`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, RollingNumber} from '@monoline/react';

function Counter() {
  const [n, setN] = useState(1204);
  return (
    <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s4)', alignItems: 'center'}}>
      <strong style={{fontSize: 'var(--display-sm)'}}><RollingNumber value={n} format={{style: 'currency', currency: 'USD', maximumFractionDigits: 0}} /></strong>
      <Button size="sm" onClick={() => setN((v) => v + 137)}>Add 137</Button>
      <Button size="sm" onClick={() => setN((v) => Math.max(0, v - 999))}>Subtract 999</Button>
    </div>
  );
}

<Counter />
```

A11y:
- The animated digits are aria-hidden; the formatted final value is plain text for screen readers.
- With prefers-reduced-motion the digits change without rolling.
- Not interactive: no focus stops.

CSS classes: rolling-number, rolling-number-visual, rolling-number-digit, rolling-number-strip, rolling-number-char
Source: registry/rolling-number.json

## Scroll area (scroll-area)
A scrollable region with thin, themed scrollbars.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Primitive: radix-ui/ScrollArea | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {ScrollArea} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal" | "both" = 'vertical' — Which scrollbars to render.
- viewportProps?: Omit<Radix.ScrollAreaViewportProps & RefAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "ref"> — Passed to the focusable viewport, e.g. a name for the region.

Usage:
```tsx
import {ScrollArea} from '@monoline/react';

<ScrollArea style={{height: '160px', width: '320px', border: '1px solid var(--rule)'}} viewportProps={{'aria-label': 'Release notes'}}><div style={{padding: 'var(--s3)'}}>{Array.from({length: 20}, (_, i) => <p key={i}>Release note {i + 1}</p>)}</div></ScrollArea>
```

A11y:
- The viewport is focusable (tabindex 0) so keyboard users can scroll it; give it an aria-label when it holds standalone content.
- Native scrolling semantics are preserved.

CSS classes: scroll-area, scroll-viewport, scroll-bar, scroll-thumb
Data attributes: data-orientation: vertical | horizontal
Source: registry/scroll-area.json

## Scroll progress (scroll-progress)
A thin bar fixed to the top of the window that fills as the page scrolls.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {ScrollProgress} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- label?: string — Give the bar a name to expose it as a `progressbar` (reading progress). Without it the bar is decorative and `aria-hidden`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {ScrollProgress} from '@monoline/react';

<ScrollProgress />
```

A11y:
- Decorative and aria-hidden by default.
- With `label` it is a progressbar with aria-valuenow from 0 to 100, updated as the page scrolls.
- No transition, so there is no motion beyond the scroll itself.

CSS classes: scroll-progress, scroll-progress-bar
Source: registry/scroll-progress.json

## Segmented control (segmented-control)
Pick exactly one option from a short row, shown as joined segments.
Status: stable | Category: buttons | Primitive: radix-ui/ToggleGroup | Related: toggle-group
Import: import {SegmentedControl} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- options: SegmentedOption[] — The segments to show, each with a `value`, a `label` and an optional `disabled`.
- value?: string — The selected segment's `value` when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string — The segment selected at first when uncontrolled. Defaults to the first option.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the new segment's `value` when the user picks a different one.
- aria-label: string — Names the control, for example "View".

Usage:
```tsx
import {SegmentedControl} from '@monoline/react';

<SegmentedControl aria-label="Chart range" options={[{value: 'day', label: 'Day'}, {value: 'week', label: 'Week'}, {value: 'month', label: 'Month'}]} defaultValue="week" />
```

A11y:
- A named radio group; arrow keys move and select, Home and End jump.
- One option is always selected: pressing the active one does nothing.

CSS classes: segmented, segment
Data attributes: data-state: on
Source: registry/segmented-control.json

## Select (select)
Pick one value from a list of five or more options.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Primitive: radix-ui/Select | Related: field
Import: import {Select} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the control invalid (`aria-invalid`). A surrounding Field sets this from its `error`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, Select, SelectContent, SelectGroup, SelectItem, SelectLabel, SelectTrigger, SelectValue} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: 320}}><Field label="Sync every"><Select defaultValue="15"><SelectTrigger><SelectValue placeholder="Choose" /></SelectTrigger><SelectContent><SelectGroup><SelectLabel>Interval</SelectLabel><SelectItem value="5">5 minutes</SelectItem><SelectItem value="15">15 minutes</SelectItem><SelectItem value="60">Hour</SelectItem></SelectGroup></SelectContent></Select></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- Trigger is role=combobox with aria-expanded; the list is role=listbox with option items.
- Arrow keys, Home, End and type-ahead move; Enter selects; Escape closes.
- Inside a Field it is labelled by the Field's label.

CSS classes: select-trigger, select-content, select-viewport, select-item, select-label, input-sm, input-lg
Data attributes: data-placeholder; data-highlighted; data-disabled; data-invalid
Source: registry/select.json

```tsx
import {Skeleton} from '@monoline/react';
```

## Slider (slider)
Pick a number, or a range, by dragging or with the keyboard.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Primitive: radix-ui/Slider | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {Slider} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: number | [number, number] — A number for one thumb, or [low, high] for a range.
- defaultValue?: number | [number, number] — The starting value when uncontrolled: a number for one thumb or `[low, high]` for a range. Default 0.
- onValueChange?: ((value: number[]) => void) — Called with an array holding the value of each thumb while the user drags or uses the keyboard.
- aria-label: string — Accessible name for each thumb. One string for a single thumb, or [low, high] labels for a range.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Slider} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s5)', maxWidth: 420}}><Slider aria-label="Volume" defaultValue={60} /><Slider aria-label="Price" defaultValue={[20, 70]} /></div>
```

A11y:
- Each thumb is role=slider with aria-valuenow, min and max.
- Arrow keys step; Home and End jump to the ends; PageUp and PageDown take larger steps.
- aria-label is required; a range labels its thumbs minimum and maximum.

CSS classes: slider, slider-track, slider-range, slider-thumb, toggle, toggle-group, range, progress
Data attributes: data-disabled; data-state: on
Source: registry/slider.json

## Sortable list (sortable-list)
A list the user reorders by dragging a handle or with the keyboard, with live announcements.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {SortableList} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label: string — Required: names the list.
- value?: SortableItem[] — The items in their current order when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: SortableItem[] = [] — The items in their starting order when uncontrolled.
- onValueChange?: ((items: SortableItem[]) => void) — Called with the new order when the user drops an item in a new place. Not called for a cancelled move or a drop where it started.
- orientation?: "vertical" | "horizontal" = 'vertical' — `vertical` (default) moves with ArrowUp and ArrowDown; `horizontal` lays the items in a row and moves with ArrowLeft and ArrowRight.

Usage:
```tsx
import {SortableList, type SortableItem} from '@monoline/react';

const items: SortableItem[] = ['Write the brief', 'Draft the spec', 'Review with design', 'Build', 'Ship'].map((t) => ({id: t, label: t}));

<div style={{maxWidth: '360px'}}><SortableList aria-label="Tasks" defaultValue={items} /></div>
```

A11y:
- Each row has a handle button named 'Reorder <item>' with aria-pressed while picked up and a description of the keys.
- Space or Enter picks an item up; the arrow keys (or Home and End) move it; Space or Enter drops it; Escape cancels and restores the order; Tab cancels.
- A polite live region announces: picked up, moved to position N of M, dropped, cancelled.
- Pointer drag uses the same handle; reordering never depends on dragging alone.

CSS classes: sortable-list, sortable-list-horizontal, sortable-list-item, sortable-list-handle, sortable-list-label
Data attributes: data-dragging
Source: registry/sortable-list.json

## Sparkline (sparkline)
A tiny inline trend line for a table cell or a sentence.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Sparkline} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- title: string — Accessible name. Required.
- data: number[] — Values in order. Non-finite values count as 0.
- labels?: string[] — Names for the values, used in the screen reader table. Default: 1, 2, 3...
- area?: boolean = false — Fill under the line.
- width?: number = 96 — Width in px. Default 96.
- height?: number = 24 — Height in px. Default 24.
- valueFormat?: ((value: number) => string) — Format a value for the screen reader table.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Sparkline} from '@monoline/react';

<p>Signups <Sparkline title="Signups, last 10 days" data={[3, 5, 4, 8, 6, 9, 12, 10, 14, 13]} /> up 18% this week.</p>
```

A11y:
- role=img with the required title as its name.
- A visually hidden table (table roles on spans, valid inside a paragraph) lists every value for screen readers.
- Decorative at a glance: it has no tooltip and no tab stops.

CSS classes: sparkline, sparkline-line, sparkline-area, sparkline-dot, sparkline-empty
Source: registry/sparkline.json

## Stack (stack)
Lay children out in a column or row with one gap from the spacing scale.
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: aspect-ratio, box, container
Import: import {Stack} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- direction?: "row" | "column" = 'column' — `column` (default) stacks children vertically; `row` lays them out horizontally.
- gap?: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 | 9 = 3 — Step on the spacing scale: 1 = --s1 (4px) up to 9.
- align?: "center" | "start" | "end" | "stretch" — Cross-axis alignment (`align-items`): `start`, `center`, `end` or `stretch`.
- justify?: "center" | "start" | "end" | "between" — Main-axis distribution (`justify-content`): `start`, `center`, `end` or `between`.
- wrap?: boolean — Lets children wrap onto new lines. Useful with `direction="row"`. Default false.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Badge, Stack} from '@monoline/react';

<Stack gap={2}><Badge>one</Badge><Badge>two</Badge><Badge>three</Badge></Stack>
```

A11y:
- A plain div; adds no roles.

CSS classes: stack, stack-row, stack-wrap
Data attributes: data-align: start | center | end | stretch; data-justify: start | center | end | between
Source: registry/stack.json

## Table (table)
Rows and columns of data with a header, in a horizontally scrolling wrapper.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Table} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
TableProps:
- wrapperLabel?: string — Names the scrollable wrapper. Give it when the table can overflow.
TableCellProps:
- numeric?: boolean — Right-aligns numbers.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow} from '@monoline/react';

<Table wrapperLabel="Team">
  <TableCaption>Team members</TableCaption>
  <TableHeader><TableRow><TableHead>Name</TableHead><TableHead>Role</TableHead><TableHead numeric>Projects</TableHead></TableRow></TableHeader>
  <TableBody>
    <TableRow><TableCell>Ada Lovelace</TableCell><TableCell>Engineer</TableCell><TableCell numeric>4</TableCell></TableRow>
    <TableRow><TableCell>Grace Hopper</TableCell><TableCell>Admiral</TableCell><TableCell numeric>9</TableCell></TableRow>
  </TableBody>
</Table>
```

A11y:
- Native table elements with th scope and an optional caption.
- The scroll wrapper is focusable and named so keyboard users can scroll wide tables.

CSS classes: table-wrap, table, num
Source: registry/table.json

Import: import {TagsInput} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: string[] — The current tags when controlled. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string[] = [] — The tags present at first when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string[]) => void) — Called with the full list of tags after one is added or removed.
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.

```tsx
import {Field, TagsInput} from '@monoline/react';
```

CSS classes: avatar, avatar-sm, avatar-lg, avatar-line, avatar-group, tag, stat, stat-value, stat-note, tags-input, tags-input-field

## Text (text)
Body text with a size and tone from the scale.
Status: stable | Category: typography | Related: heading, kbd, link
Import: import {Text} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" | "xs" = 'md' — Type size: `xs`, `sm`, `md` (default) or `lg`.
- tone?: "success" | "warning" | "danger" | "accent" | "default" | "muted" | "ok" = 'default' — Colour role: `default`, `muted`, `success`, `warning`, `danger` or `accent`, the same names as Alert. Never rely on colour alone to carry meaning. `ok` still works.
- truncate?: boolean — One line with an ellipsis.
- asChild?: boolean — Render the child (a span, label, li) with the text styles.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Text} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 'var(--s2)'}}><Text size="lg">Large</Text><Text>Medium</Text><Text size="sm" tone="muted">Small and muted</Text><Text size="xs" tone="danger">Extra small, danger</Text></div>
```

A11y:
- A plain p (or the child with asChild); tone is never the only signal, so pair danger text with words.

CSS classes: text, text-xs, text-sm, text-md, text-lg, text-muted, text-danger, text-success, text-ok, text-warning, text-accent, text-truncate
Source: registry/text.json

## Theme provider (theme-provider)
Set and save the theme, accent, font, corners, density and direction from React with useTheme(), and avoid the first-paint flash with themeScript().
Status: stable | Category: layout | Related: direction-provider, native-select
Import: import {ThemeProvider} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- storageKey?: string = 'monoline' — Prefix of the localStorage keys, e.g. `monoline` stores `monoline-theme`. Default "monoline". Match it in `themeScript`.
- children?: ReactNode — The app.
- theme?: Theme
- accent?: Accent
- font?: Font
- radius?: Radius
- density?: Density
- dir?: Dir

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, ThemeProvider, ThemeSwitcher, useTheme} from '@monoline/react';

function Controls() {
  const {theme, resolvedTheme, accent, density, setTheme, setDensity} = useTheme();
  return (
    <div style={{display: 'grid', gap: 12}}>
      <ThemeSwitcher />
      <p>Theme: {theme}{theme === 'system' ? ` (${resolvedTheme})` : ''}. Accent: {accent}. Density: {density}.</p>
      <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 8}}>
        <Button onClick={() => setTheme(resolvedTheme === 'dark' ? 'warm' : 'dark')}>Toggle dark</Button>
        <Button onClick={() => setDensity(density === 'compact' ? 'comfortable' : 'compact')}>Toggle compact</Button>
      </div>
    </div>
  );
}

<ThemeProvider storageKey="monoline-demo"><Controls /></ThemeProvider>
```

A11y:
- The theme follows the system colour scheme until the user chooses one.
- ThemeSwitcher is a labelled group of native selects, fully keyboard operable.
- Changing direction also sets dir on the page so arrow keys follow the reading direction.
Source: registry/theme-provider.json

## Time field (time-field)
Hour, minute and AM/PM segments you step with arrow keys or type into.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: autocomplete, calendar, checkbox
Import: import {TimeField} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: string — The time as 24-hour `"HH:mm"` when controlled; `""` means none. Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string — The initial time as `"HH:mm"` when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with `"HH:mm"` once hour and minute are both set, or `""` when either is cleared.
- hourCycle?: 12 | 24 = 12 — Show hours 1-12 with an AM/PM segment (`12`) or 0-23 (`24`). Default 12.
- step?: number = 1 — Minutes the arrow keys move by. Default 1.
- disabled?: boolean — Stops all input.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.
- name?: string — Form field name; a hidden input submits the 24-hour `"HH:mm"` value.
- aria-label?: string — Names the group when it is not inside a Field. Default "Time".

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, TimeField} from '@monoline/react';

<Field label="Start time"><TimeField defaultValue="09:30" /></Field>
```

A11y:
- A named group of spin buttons (Hour, Minute, AM or PM), each with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax and aria-valuetext.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown step a segment (minutes by the step prop), PageUp/PageDown step further, Home/End jump to the limits, Backspace clears.
- Typing digits fills a segment and moves to the next; A and P set AM and PM.
- ArrowLeft/ArrowRight move between segments and are mirrored in right-to-left.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, time-field, time-segment, time-sep
Data attributes: data-empty; data-disabled
Source: registry/time-field.json

## Time picker (time-picker)
Pick a time of day with hour, minute and AM/PM segments, using the browser's own control.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: input, field
Import: import {TimePicker} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: string — 24-hour "HH:mm" (or "HH:mm:ss" when `step` is under 60), or '' for no time.
- defaultValue?: string = '' — The initial time as 24-hour "HH:mm" when uncontrolled. Default empty.
- onValueChange?: ((value: string) => void) — Called with the new time as 24-hour "HH:mm" (or '' when cleared).
- size?: "sm" | "md" | "lg" = 'md' — `md` (default), `sm` for dense layouts or `lg` for prominent forms. Heights match Button, Input and Select at each size.
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the control invalid (`aria-invalid`). A surrounding Field sets this from its `error`.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, TimePicker} from '@monoline/react';

<div style={{maxWidth: '200px'}}><Field label="Start time"><TimePicker defaultValue="09:30" /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- Native input type="time": the browser exposes hour, minute and AM/PM as spinbuttons.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown change a segment, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight or Tab move between segments, typing digits fills one.
- The control takes its name from a label or aria-label; min, max and step are passed through.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, time-picker
Source: registry/time-picker.json

## Toast (toast)
A short message that appears briefly and does not block the page.
Status: stable | Category: feedback | Primitive: radix-ui/Toast | Related: alert, empty-state, notification-center
Import: import {Toast} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, Toast, ToastAction, ToastClose, ToastDescription, ToastProvider, ToastTitle, ToastViewport} from '@monoline/react';

function Example() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <ToastProvider duration={5000}>
      <Button onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Save draft</Button>
      <Toast open={open} onOpenChange={setOpen}>
        <ToastTitle>Draft saved</ToastTitle>
        <ToastDescription>Stored on this device.</ToastDescription>
        <ToastAction altText="Undo the save">Undo</ToastAction>
        <ToastClose />
      </Toast>
      <ToastViewport label="Notifications" />
    </ToastProvider>
  );
}

<Example />
```

A11y:
- Announced politely by assistive tech without moving focus.
- Pauses its timer on hover and focus; F8 jumps focus to the toast region.
- Never the only place a critical result appears; keep an inline message too.

CSS classes: toast-viewport, toast-item, toast-title, toast-description, toast-action, toast-close
Data attributes: data-state: open | closed
Source: registry/toast.json

## Toaster (toaster)
Show a toast from anywhere with toast('Saved'). Mount one Toaster; call toast.success, toast.error or toast.promise from handlers.
Status: stable | Category: feedback | Related: toast
Import: import {Toaster} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- limit?: number = 3 — Most toasts shown at once. Older ones wait out of sight and return when there is room. Default 3.
- position?: "center" | "start" | "end" = 'end' — Where the stack sits. `end` is the bottom corner at the end of the reading direction. Default "end".
- label?: string = 'Notifications' — Names the region for screen readers. Default "Notifications".
- dismissLabel?: string = 'Dismiss' — Text of each close button. Default "Dismiss".

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Toaster, toast} from '@monoline/react';

function Example() {
  return (
    <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 8, flexWrap: 'wrap'}}>
      <Button onClick={() => toast('Draft saved')}>Default</Button>
      <Button onClick={() => toast.success('Profile updated', {description: 'Changes are live.'})}>Success</Button>
      <Button onClick={() => toast.error('Could not save', {description: 'Check your connection.', action: {label: 'Retry', onClick: () => toast.info('Retrying')}})}>Error with retry</Button>
      <Button onClick={() => toast.warning('Storage almost full')}>Warning</Button>
      <Button onClick={() => toast.promise(new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, 1500)), {loading: 'Uploading', success: 'Uploaded', error: 'Upload failed'})}>Promise</Button>
      <Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => toast.dismiss()}>Dismiss all</Button>
      <Toaster />
    </div>
  );
}

<Example />
```

A11y:
- Info and success toasts are announced politely; errors are announced assertively.
- F8 moves focus to the notification region; hovering or focusing a toast pauses its timer.
- Each toast has a Dismiss button and an optional action button; Escape closes the focused toast.
- A stack limit keeps at most three visible by default (older ones wait); motion is removed with prefers-reduced-motion.
- Never the only place a critical result appears; keep an inline message too.

CSS classes: toast-viewport, toast-item, toast-title, toast-description, toast-action, toast-close, toaster-viewport, toaster-item
Data attributes: data-state: open | closed; data-position: start | center; data-kind: success | warning | error | loading; data-swipe: move | cancel
Source: registry/toaster.json

## Tooltip (tooltip)
Short hint text on hover and keyboard focus.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Primitive: radix-ui/Tooltip | Related: alert-dialog, command, context-menu
Import: import {Tooltip} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- content: ReactNode — The text shown. Keep it short; it repeats or extends a label and must never hold essential information alone.
- children: ReactNode — The trigger element. It receives aria-describedby when open.
- side?: "top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left" = 'top' — Which side of the trigger the tooltip appears on: `top` (default), `right`, `bottom` or `left`.
- delayDuration?: number — Milliseconds to wait before showing on hover. Defaults to the `TooltipProvider` value.
- open?: boolean — Whether the tooltip is open when controlled. Pair with `onOpenChange`.
- defaultOpen?: boolean — Whether the tooltip starts open when uncontrolled. Default false.
- onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Called with the new open state when the tooltip shows or hides.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, Tooltip, TooltipProvider} from '@monoline/react';

<TooltipProvider><div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)'}}><Tooltip content="Saved to ~/Notes"><Button>Save</Button></Tooltip><Tooltip content="Below" side="bottom"><Button>Bottom</Button></Tooltip></div></TooltipProvider>
```

A11y:
- Shows on hover and on keyboard focus; the trigger gets aria-describedby while it is open.
- Escape dismisses it; it stays open while the pointer is over it.
- Never the only place for essential information: touch users do not get hover.

CSS classes: tooltip
Source: registry/tooltip.json

## Tour (tour)
A guided walkthrough: a spotlight on one element at a time with a card and Next, Back and Skip.
Status: stable | Category: overlays | Related: alert-dialog, command, context-menu
Import: import {Tour} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- steps: TourStep[] — The steps, in order.
- open?: boolean — Whether the tour is showing, when controlled. Pair with `onOpenChange`.
- defaultOpen?: boolean = false — Whether the tour starts open when uncontrolled. Default false.
- onOpenChange?: ((open: boolean) => void) — Called with false when the tour ends: Skip, Escape or Done.
- step?: number — The current step index when controlled. Pair with `onStepChange`.
- defaultStep?: number = 0 — The step to start on when uncontrolled. Default 0.
- onStepChange?: ((step: number) => void) — Called with the new index when the user moves between steps.
- onFinish?: (() => void) — Called when the user finishes the last step (not when they skip or press Escape).
- spotlightPadding?: number = 6 — Extra space in px around the highlighted element. Default 6.
- labels?: TourLabels — Replaces the button text.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Tour} from '@monoline/react';

function Basic() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  return (
    <div>
      <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s4)', alignItems: 'center'}}>
        <button type="button" className="btn btn-solid" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Start tour</button>
        <button type="button" className="btn" id="tour-demo-a">Create</button>
        <button type="button" className="btn" id="tour-demo-b">Share</button>
      </div>
      <Tour
        open={open}
        onOpenChange={setOpen}
        steps={[
          {target: '#tour-demo-a', title: 'Create', content: 'Start a new project from here.'},
          {target: '#tour-demo-b', title: 'Share', content: 'Invite people by email.', placement: 'end'},
          {title: 'That is all', content: 'You can restart the tour at any time.'},
        ]}
      />
    </div>
  );
}

<Basic />
```

A11y:
- The step card is a dialog named by its title and described by its text; it takes focus on every step.
- Tab stays inside the card; Escape ends the tour and focus returns to where it was.
- ArrowRight and ArrowLeft move between steps when the card has focus (mirrored in right-to-left).
- Each step is announced politely as "Step n of m"; the highlighted element scrolls into view.
- The overlay and spotlight are hidden from assistive technology; animation stops under prefers-reduced-motion.

CSS classes: btn, btn-solid, btn-line, btn-danger, btn-ghost, btn-sm, btn-lg, btn-block, tour, tour-overlay, tour-spotlight, tour-card, tour-count, tour-title, tour-content, tour-actions, tour-spacer
Source: registry/tour.json

## Tree (tree)
A nested list of items that open and close, with one selected item.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {Tree} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- items: TreeNode[] — The top-level nodes; each node has an `id`, a `label` and optional `children`.
- value?: string — Selected node id. Controlled with `value` + `onValueChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultValue`.
- defaultValue?: string — The id of the node selected at first when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onValueChange?: ((id: string) => void) — Called with the id of the node the user selects.
- expanded?: string[] — Open branches. Controlled with `expanded` + `onExpandedChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultExpanded`.
- defaultExpanded?: string[] = [] — Ids of the branches open at first when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onExpandedChange?: ((ids: string[]) => void) — Called with the full list of open branch ids when the user opens or closes a branch.
- aria-label: string — Required: names the tree.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Tree, type TreeNode} from '@monoline/react';

const items: TreeNode[] = [
  {id: 'src', label: 'src', children: [
    {id: 'components', label: 'components', children: [{id: 'button', label: 'button.tsx'}, {id: 'tree', label: 'tree.tsx'}]},
    {id: 'index', label: 'index.ts'},
  ]},
  {id: 'docs', label: 'docs', children: [{id: 'readme', label: 'README.md'}]},
  {id: 'pkg', label: 'package.json'},
];

<Tree aria-label="Project files" items={items} defaultExpanded={['src', 'components']} />
```

A11y:
- role=tree with treeitem children and role=group for branches; aria-expanded on branches, aria-selected on every item, aria-level on each.
- Roving tabindex: one item is in the tab order; Tab enters and leaves the tree as one stop.
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown move, ArrowRight opens a branch then enters it, ArrowLeft closes it then goes to the parent, Home and End jump.
- Enter or Space selects; typing letters jumps to the next label that starts with them. The tree needs an aria-label.

CSS classes: tree, tree-group, tree-item, tree-row, tree-twisty
Data attributes: data-selected
Source: registry/tree.json

## Tree select (tree-select)
A select whose options are a nested tree, with search and single or multiple selection.
Status: stable | Category: forms | Related: tree, combobox, input
Import: import {TreeSelect} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- items: TreeNode[] — The tree: top-level nodes, each with an `id`, a `label` and optional `children`. Same shape as `Tree`.
- value?: string[] — Selected node ids when controlled. Always an array, also in single mode (zero or one id). Pair with `onValueChange`.
- defaultValue?: string[] = [] — Ids selected at first when uncontrolled. Default none.
- onValueChange?: ((ids: string[]) => void) — Called with the full list of selected ids after each change.
- multiple?: boolean = false — Allows several selections: choosing a node toggles it and the list stays open. Default false (choosing closes the list).
- emptyText?: string = 'No matches' — Shown when the search matches nothing. Default "No matches".
- invalid?: boolean — Marks the field as having an error: sets `aria-invalid` and shows the error border.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Field, TreeSelect, type TreeNode} from '@monoline/react';

const items: TreeNode[] = [
  {id: 'eng', label: 'Engineering', children: [
    {id: 'web', label: 'Web'},
    {id: 'platform', label: 'Platform', children: [{id: 'infra', label: 'Infrastructure'}, {id: 'data', label: 'Data'}]},
  ]},
  {id: 'design', label: 'Design', children: [{id: 'brand', label: 'Brand'}, {id: 'product', label: 'Product design'}]},
  {id: 'ops', label: 'Operations'},
];

<div style={{maxWidth: '320px', minHeight: '300px'}}><Field label="Team"><TreeSelect items={items} placeholder="Choose a team" /></Field></div>
```

A11y:
- An input with role=combobox, aria-haspopup=tree and aria-activedescendant; focus never leaves the input.
- The popup is role=tree: each treeitem has aria-level, aria-setsize, aria-posinset, aria-selected and (for branches) aria-expanded; aria-multiselectable in multiple mode.
- ArrowDown/ArrowUp open the list and move; ArrowRight opens a branch then enters it; ArrowLeft closes it then goes to the parent (swapped in RTL); Enter selects or toggles; Escape closes.
- Typing filters the tree to matching nodes and their parents, opened automatically; an empty result shows text.
- Selection is shown in the input as text ('A, B' or '3 selected') and a check mark, not colour.

CSS classes: field, field-hint, input, select, textarea, input-sm, input-lg, input-wrap, input-end, input-bare, switch, setting, seg, muted, seg-opt, tree-select, tree-select-list, tree-select-item, tree-select-twisty, tree-select-empty
Data attributes: data-active
Source: registry/tree-select.json

## Typewriter (typewriter)
Type a string one character at a time. Static for reduced motion.
Status: stable | Category: effects | Related: animated-list, bento-grid, border-beam
Import: import {Typewriter} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- text: string — The string to type. Screen readers get all of it at once.
- speed?: number = 40 — Milliseconds per character. Default 40.
- delay?: number = 0 — Milliseconds to wait before the first character. Default 0.
- cursor?: boolean = true — Show a blinking caret. Default true.
- onComplete?: (() => void) — Called once the last character is shown (also straight away for reduced motion).

Usage:
```tsx
import {Typewriter} from '@monoline/react';

<p style={{fontFamily: 'var(--font-display)', fontSize: 'var(--display-sm)'}}><Typewriter text="Small parts, drawn with thin lines." /></p>
```

A11y:
- Screen readers get the full text at once from an sr-only copy; the typed characters are aria-hidden.
- With prefers-reduced-motion the full text shows immediately and the caret does not blink.

CSS classes: typewriter-caret
Source: registry/typewriter.json

## Virtual list (virtual-list)
A windowed list for thousands of rows: only the rows in view are in the page.
Status: stable | Category: data-display | Related: accordion, area-chart, avatar
Import: import {VirtualList} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- aria-label: string — Required: names the list for screen readers.
- count: number — How many rows the whole list has, rendered or not.
- itemHeight: number — Height of every row in pixels. All rows share it.
- height: number — Height of the scrolling window in pixels.
- overscan?: number = 4 — Extra rows rendered above and below the visible ones, so fast scrolling shows no blanks. Default 4.
- renderItem: (index: number) => ReactNode — Returns the content of row `index`. Only called for rows in or near the window.

Usage:
```tsx
import {VirtualList} from '@monoline/react';

<VirtualList aria-label="Ten thousand rows" count={10000} itemHeight={32} height={192} renderItem={(i) => <span className="virtual-list-cell">Row {i + 1}</span>} />
```

A11y:
- role=list with listitem rows; every row carries aria-posinset and aria-setsize so the position in the full list is announced.
- Roving tabindex: one row is in the tab order. ArrowUp/ArrowDown, PageUp/PageDown, Home and End move focus and scroll the row into view.
- The list needs an aria-label.

CSS classes: virtual-list, virtual-list-body, virtual-list-row
Source: registry/virtual-list.json

## useClickOutside (use-click-outside)
Calls a function when a pointer goes down outside an element, to close menus and popovers.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-clipboard, use-controllable-state, use-counter
Import: import {useClickOutside} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, useClickOutside} from '@monoline/react';

function PopoverDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const ref = useClickOutside<HTMLDivElement>(() => setOpen(false), open);
  return (
    <div>
      <Button variant="line" aria-expanded={open} onClick={() => setOpen((o) => !o)}>Open panel</Button>
      {open && (
        <div ref={ref} role="group" aria-label="Panel">
          <p>Click anywhere outside this panel to close it.</p>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

<PopoverDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Close popovers with Escape too; this hook covers pointer only.
- Listens to pointerdown on the document and removes the listener on unmount.
Source: registry/use-click-outside.json

## useClipboard (use-clipboard)
Copy text with the Clipboard API, with a copied flag that resets after a delay and an error when it fails.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-controllable-state, use-counter
Import: import {useClipboard} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
UseClipboardOptions:
- timeout?: number = 2000 — How long `copied` stays true, in milliseconds. Default 2000.
UseClipboardReturn:
- copied: boolean — True for `timeout` ms after a successful copy.
- error: Error | null — The last failure, cleared by the next copy.
- copy: (value: string) => Promise<boolean> — Copies text. Resolves `true` on success, `false` on failure (never throws).

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, useClipboard} from '@monoline/react';

function ClipboardDemo() {
  const {copied, error, copy} = useClipboard();
  return (
    <div>
      <Button variant="line" onClick={() => copy('npm install @monoline/react')}>
        {copied ? 'Copied' : 'Copy install command'}
      </Button>
      {error && <p role="status">Copy failed. Select the text and copy it yourself.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}

<ClipboardDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Pair the copied state with a visible or aria-live status message in the UI.
- A failed copy returns false and sets error; it never throws.
Source: registry/use-clipboard.json

## useControllableState (use-controllable-state)
The value, defaultValue and onChange pattern for custom components that can be controlled or uncontrolled.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-counter
Import: import {useControllableState} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- value?: T — When defined, the hook is controlled and `value` wins.
- defaultValue: T — Starting value when uncontrolled.
- onChange?: ((value: T) => void) — Called with the new value when it differs from the current one.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, useControllableState} from '@monoline/react';

interface CounterProps {
  value?: number;
  defaultValue?: number;
  onValueChange?: (value: number) => void;
}

function Counter({value, defaultValue = 0, onValueChange}: CounterProps) {
  const [count, setCount] = useControllableState({value, defaultValue, onChange: onValueChange});
  return (
    <div>
      <Button variant="line" aria-label="Decrease" onClick={() => setCount(count - 1)}>−</Button>{' '}
      <output>{count}</output>{' '}
      <Button variant="line" aria-label="Increase" onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>+</Button>
    </div>
  );
}

<Counter defaultValue={2} />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Lets a custom widget accept value/defaultValue/onValueChange like the Monoline components do.
- onChange fires only when the new value differs from the current one.
Source: registry/use-controllable-state.json

## useCounter (use-counter)
A number with increment, decrement, set and reset, bounded by optional min and max.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useCounter} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- min?: number
- max?: number

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, useCounter} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const {count, increment, decrement, reset} = useCounter(1, {min: 0, max: 5});
  return <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', alignItems: 'center'}}><Button onClick={() => decrement()} disabled={count === 0}>Less</Button><output aria-live="polite">{count}</output><Button onClick={() => increment()} disabled={count === 5}>More</Button><Button variant="ghost" onClick={reset}>Reset</Button></div>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output.
Source: registry/use-counter.json

## useDebounce (use-debounce)
Debounced value and debounced callback: wait for input to settle before acting.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useDebounce} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- call: (...args: A) => void — Schedules `fn` to run `delay` ms after the last call.
- cancel: () => void — Drops the pending call, if any.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {useDebounce} from '@monoline/react';

function SearchDemo() {
  const [query, setQuery] = useState('');
  const settled = useDebounce(query, 400);
  return (
    <div>
      <label>
        Search
        <input value={query} onChange={(e) => setQuery(e.target.value)} />
      </label>
      <p>Searching for: {settled || '…'}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

<SearchDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Use for search fields so the list updates after typing stops.
- A pending callback is dropped on unmount.
Source: registry/use-debounce.json

## useDisclosure (use-disclosure)
Open and closed state with open, close and toggle functions, and callbacks when it changes.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useDisclosure} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
UseDisclosureOptions:
- initialOpen?: boolean = false — Open on first render. Default `false`.
- onOpen?: (() => void) — Called when the state changes from closed to open. Not called on mount.
- onClose?: (() => void) — Called when the state changes from open to closed. Not called on mount.
UseDisclosureReturn:
- isOpen: boolean
- open: () => void
- close: () => void
- toggle: () => void

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, useDisclosure} from '@monoline/react';

function DisclosureDemo() {
  const {isOpen, toggle} = useDisclosure();
  return (
    <div>
      <Button variant="line" aria-expanded={isOpen} onClick={toggle}>{isOpen ? 'Hide details' : 'Show details'}</Button>
      {isOpen && <p>Details appear here.</p>}
    </div>
  );
}

<DisclosureDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Pair with aria-expanded and aria-controls on the trigger.
- Callbacks run only when the state actually changes, not on mount.
Source: registry/use-disclosure.json

Set document.title while a component is mounted, then restore it.

A11y:

## useFocusTrap (use-focus-trap)
Keeps Tab focus inside an element while it is active, and returns focus when it closes.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useFocusTrap} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, useFocusTrap} from '@monoline/react';

function TrapDemo() {
  const [open, setOpen] = useState(false);
  const ref = useFocusTrap<HTMLDivElement>(open);
  return (
    <div>
      <Button variant="line" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>Open trapped panel</Button>
      {open && (
        <div ref={ref} role="dialog" aria-label="Trapped panel">
          <p>Tab stays inside this panel.</p>
          <Button variant="line" onClick={() => setOpen(false)}>Close</Button>
          <Button variant="ghost">Second action</Button>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

<TrapDemo />
```

A11y:
- Tab and Shift+Tab cycle inside the container while active. Focus moves in on activation.
- Focus returns to the element that had it before when the trap ends. Escape to close is the caller's job.
Source: registry/use-focus-trap.json

Read and set location.hash as state.

```tsx
function Demo() {
```
