## useHotkeys (use-hotkeys)
Keyboard shortcuts such as mod+k or escape, ignored while typing in fields unless allowed.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useHotkeys} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- enabled?: boolean = true — Set false to turn every binding off. Default true.
- allowInInputs?: boolean = false — Also fire while focus is in a text field, select or contenteditable. Default false.
- preventDefault?: boolean = true — Call `preventDefault` on a matched key. Default true.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {useHotkeys} from '@monoline/react';

function HotkeysDemo() {
  const [last, setLast] = useState('none yet');
  useHotkeys({
    'mod+k': () => setLast('mod+k'),
    'shift+h': () => setLast('shift+h'),
    escape: () => setLast('escape'),
  });
  return (
    <div>
      <p>Press Mod+K (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere), Shift+H or Escape.</p>
      <p>Last shortcut: {last}</p>
    </div>
  );
}

<HotkeysDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Shortcuts are additions: every control must still be reachable by keyboard and Tab.
- mod means Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere. Typing in inputs is ignored unless allowInInputs is set.
Source: registry/use-hotkeys.json

## useHover (use-hover)
Track whether the pointer is over an element.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useHover} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

```tsx
import {useHover} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [ref, hovered] = useHover<HTMLDivElement>();
  return <div ref={ref} style={{padding: 'var(--s5)', border: '1px solid var(--rule)', background: hovered ? 'var(--wash-2)' : 'transparent'}}>{hovered ? 'Pointer is over this box' : 'Move the pointer here'}</div>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Hover is pointer-only: never hide essential content or actions behind it.
Source: registry/use-hover.json

## useIntersection (use-intersection)
Know whether an element is in view, with an IntersectionObserver.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useIntersection} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):
- once?: boolean — Stop observing after the first time it is visible.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useIntersection} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [ref, entry] = useIntersection<HTMLDivElement>({threshold: 0.5});
  return (
    <div style={{height: '120px', overflowY: 'auto', border: '1px solid var(--rule)'}} tabIndex={0} aria-label="Scrollable area">
      <div style={{height: '160px', padding: 'var(--s3)'}}>Scroll down</div>
      <div ref={ref} style={{padding: 'var(--s4)', background: entry?.isIntersecting ? 'var(--wash-2)' : 'transparent'}}>{entry?.isIntersecting ? 'In view' : 'Out of view'}</div>
      <div style={{height: '120px'}} />
    </div>
  );
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. When IntersectionObserver is unavailable, it reports not intersecting.
Source: registry/use-intersection.json

## useInterval (use-interval)
Calls a function on a timer, with a null delay to pause it. Cleared on unmount.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useInterval} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, useInterval} from '@monoline/react';

function IntervalDemo() {
  const [running, setRunning] = useState(true);
  const [seconds, setSeconds] = useState(0);
  useInterval(() => setSeconds((s) => s + 1), running ? 1000 : null);
  return (
    <div>
      <p>Elapsed: {seconds} s</p>
      <Button variant="line" onClick={() => setRunning((r) => !r)}>{running ? 'Pause' : 'Resume'}</Button>
    </div>
  );
}

<IntervalDemo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output. Clears its timer on unmount so nothing runs after the component is gone.
- Pass null as the delay to pause.
Source: registry/use-interval.json

## useLocalStorage (use-local-storage)
A JSON value kept in localStorage, shaped like useState, that stays in sync across tabs.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useLocalStorage} from '@monoline/react'

```tsx
      <Button variant="line" onClick={() => setCount((n) => n + 1)}>Count is {count}</Button>

    </div>
  );
}

<CountDemo />
```

A11y:

## useLongPress (use-long-press)
Call a handler when an element is held down, cancelling if the pointer moves or lifts early.

Import: import {useLongPress} from '@monoline/react'

Props (name: type = default, ? means optional):


A11y:
- Press and hold is hard for many people: always offer a normal click or keyboard action for the same result.

## useTimeout (use-timeout)
Run a callback after a delay, with start and clear controls.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useTimeout} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {Button, useTimeout} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [msg, setMsg] = useState('Idle');
  const {start, clear} = useTimeout(() => setMsg('Done after one second'), 1000);
  return <div style={{display: 'flex', gap: 'var(--s3)', alignItems: 'center'}}><Button onClick={() => { setMsg('Waiting'); start(); }}>Start</Button><Button variant="ghost" onClick={() => { clear(); setMsg('Cancelled'); }}>Cancel</Button><output aria-live="polite">{msg}</output></div>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output.
Source: registry/use-timeout.json

## useToggle (use-toggle)
Cycle through a list of values, or flip a boolean.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useToggle} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {Button, useToggle} from '@monoline/react';

const themes = ['warm', 'dark', 'midnight'] as const;

function Demo() {
  const [theme, next] = useToggle<string>(themes as unknown as readonly [string, ...string[]]);
  return <Button onClick={() => next()}>Theme: {theme}</Button>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output.
Source: registry/use-toggle.json

## useWindowEvent (use-window-event)
Add a typed window event listener that is removed on unmount.
Status: stable | Category: hooks | Related: use-click-outside, use-clipboard, use-controllable-state
Import: import {useWindowEvent} from '@monoline/react'

Props: no exported *Props type in the source. Extra props go to the underlying element or primitive.

Usage:
```tsx
import {useState} from 'react';
import {useWindowEvent} from '@monoline/react';

function Demo() {
  const [key, setKey] = useState('none');
  useWindowEvent('keydown', (e) => setKey(e.key));
  return <p>Last key pressed: <kbd className="kbd">{key}</kbd></p>;
}

<Demo />
```

A11y:
- No DOM output.
Source: registry/use-window-event.json
